test-keyboard.s3b: Each working key turns pink; the key you hold turns dark. Go row by row so you do not miss any. Tab moves on after you have tested it once.
test-keyboard.s4b: Last key shows key, code, keyCode, location (left, right or numpad) and modifiers. Left and right Shift have different codes, so you can tell them apart.
test-keyboard.s5b: Hold several keys together, for example W, A, S and Shift. The counter shows the most held at once. If a key does not light up while others are down, the keyboard has a rollover limit.
test-keyboard.s6b: Keys still white after a full pass did not register: try them in a text field too. A key that stays dark is stuck. Reset clears the map for another pass.
test-keyboard.diagram1: key = character, code = physical key, keyCode = legacy number.
test-keyboard.diagram2: Hold W + A + S + Shift: most at once shows the rollover.

find-zodiac-sign.name: How to find your star sign and Chinese zodiac animal
find-zodiac-sign.blurb: Your star sign depends on the day and month; your Chinese zodiac animal on the lunar year, which starts on Lunar New Year between 21 January and 20 February. 15 August 1995 is Leo and the wood Pig.
find-zodiac-sign.title: How to find your star sign and Chinese zodiac animal
find-zodiac-sign.lead: You want your star sign, your Chinese zodiac animal, or both. You will enter a birthday and read both, with the Lunar New Year date checked for early-year birthdays. Nothing leaves this tab.
find-zodiac-sign.result: Star sign with its dates and element, Chinese zodiac animal, year element with yin or yang, and the year name.
find-zodiac-sign.note: Open the zodiac sign finder with the birth date in day, month and year. Nothing is uploaded.
find-zodiac-sign.s1b: The star sign follows the Sun through 12 signs, so it depends only on the day and month: Leo runs from 23 July to 22 August. The Chinese zodiac gives each lunar year one of 12 animals, so it depends on the year.
find-zodiac-sign.s2t: Open Zodiac sign finder on cv.cm
find-zodiac-sign.s2b: A sample birthday, 15 August 1995, shows Leo and the wood Pig. Below are tables of sign dates and animal years. Nothing is uploaded.
find-zodiac-sign.s3b: Pick the date. Star sign, dates, element, Chinese zodiac, year element and year name update at once.
find-zodiac-sign.s4b: The lunar year starts on Lunar New Year, between 21 January and 20 February. 9 February 2024 is still the Rabbit, because the Dragon year began on 10 February. The tool says when a birthday falls before it.
find-zodiac-sign.s5t: Read the element and year name
find-zodiac-sign.s5b: Each year has an element (wood, fire, earth, metal or water) and is yin or yang; with the animal they form a 60-year cycle such as 甲辰 (wood Dragon) for 2024.
find-zodiac-sign.s6b: If you were born on the first or last day of a sign, it can move by a day in some years. Copy puts all the results on the clipboard.
find-zodiac-sign.diagram1: Star sign = day and month; Chinese zodiac = lunar year.
find-zodiac-sign.diagram2: 9 Feb 2024 = Rabbit; 10 Feb 2024 = Dragon (Lunar New Year).

test-click-speed.name: How to test your click speed (CPS)
test-click-speed.blurb: Click as fast as you can for 5 seconds, read your clicks per second and compare it with typical scores. Nothing is uploaded.
test-click-speed.title: How to test your click speed (CPS)
test-click-speed.lead: You want to know how fast you click, for a game or just for fun. You will run a timed CPS test, read the score and try a faster clicking technique. Clicks are counted in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
test-click-speed.result: Your clicks per second for the chosen length, your total clicks and your best score this session.
test-click-speed.note: Use the mouse you play with. Take short breaks: fast clicking for long stretches strains the hand and wrist.
test-click-speed.s1b: CPS is clicks per second: total clicks divided by the seconds of the test. 35 clicks in 5 seconds is 7 CPS. Most people click 5–8 CPS with one finger.
test-click-speed.s2b: The big pad below the options says “Click here to start”. Length is set to 5 seconds, the usual test.
test-click-speed.s3b: Choose 1 second for a short burst or 30–60 seconds to test how long you keep the pace. Your best score is kept per length.
test-click-speed.s4t: Click as fast as you can
test-click-speed.s4b: The timer starts with your first click. Time left, Clicks and Clicks per second update live. Clicks after time runs out do not count.
test-click-speed.s5b: You get your CPS and total clicks with a speed band: under 5 relaxed, 5–8 typical, 8–11 fast, 11+ very fast. Copy result puts it on the clipboard.
test-click-speed.s6b: Jitter clicking tenses the forearm so the finger vibrates; butterfly clicking alternates two fingers on one button. Both can reach 10–15 CPS. Rest if your hand hurts.
test-click-speed.diagram1: CPS = clicks ÷ seconds: 35 clicks in 5 s = 7 CPS.

test-reaction-time.name: How to test your reaction time
test-reaction-time.blurb: Click as soon as the screen turns green, five times, and read your average and median reaction time in milliseconds. Nothing is uploaded.
test-reaction-time.title: How to test your reaction time
test-reaction-time.lead: You want to measure how quickly you respond to something you see — for gaming, sport or curiosity. You will run five tries, avoid false starts and read a fair average. Timing happens in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
test-reaction-time.result: Five reaction times in ms with the average, median, best and worst, and how they compare with a typical score.
test-reaction-time.note: Close heavy apps and tabs, sit as you normally would and use the same device each time you compare results.
test-reaction-time.s1b: Reaction time is the delay between a signal and your response. For a visual signal and a click, most people score about 200–300 ms; under 200 ms is fast.
test-reaction-time.s2t: Open Reaction time test on cv.cm
test-reaction-time.s2b: The big pad says “Click to start”. Mouse, touch, Space or Enter all work.
test-reaction-time.s3b: After you click, the pad turns red and shows “Wait for green…”. The wait is random, 1.5 to 4.5 seconds, so you cannot guess it.
test-reaction-time.s4b: When the pad turns green and says “Click!”, click at once. Your time appears in ms. If you click while it is red you see “Too soon” and the try does not count.
test-reaction-time.s5b: Click again for each try. After five, Results shows the average, median, best and worst. The median ignores one unusually slow or fast try.
test-reaction-time.s6b: Screens, mice and browsers add a few to tens of ms, so compare on the same device. Rest, warm up with a few tries, and take the median of several rounds.
test-reaction-time.diagram1: Red → random 1.5–4.5 s → green → click = your time.

generate-test-tone.name: How to play a test tone
generate-test-tone.blurb: Play a pure tone at any frequency, send it to the left or right speaker and sweep the range to test speakers, headphones and your hearing. Runs in your browser.
generate-test-tone.title: How to play a test tone to check speakers and headphones
generate-test-tone.lead: You want to check that both speakers work, find a rattle, tune to A4 or see how high you can hear. You will play a sine tone, change its frequency and send it to one side at a time. The sound is made in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
generate-test-tone.result: A steady tone at the frequency you choose, on the left, right or both speakers, with its nearest musical note.
generate-test-tone.note: Turn the device volume down before you press Play, especially with headphones. High tones can be unpleasant even when quiet.
generate-test-tone.s1b: Frequency is vibrations per second, in hertz (Hz). People hear roughly 20 Hz to 20 kHz; the top end falls with age, often to 15–17 kHz for adults. 440 Hz is the note A4.
generate-test-tone.s2b: It is set to 440 Hz, a sine wave, both speakers and 20% volume. Press Play and raise the volume slowly; press Stop to end it.
generate-test-tone.s3b: Type a value, drag the slider, use −1/+1 for small steps or ÷2/×2 to move an octave. Presets give 440 Hz, middle C, 1000 Hz and more.
generate-test-tone.s4b: Under Speaker pick Left, then Right. Each side should play alone; if both play, check that the speakers are not set to mono.
generate-test-tone.s5b: Slowly move the slider from 50 Hz up. A buzz at one frequency points to a loose part; where a tone fades out is your speaker's (or hearing's) limit.
generate-test-tone.s6b: Square, triangle and sawtooth add harmonics and sound buzzier. Use sine for measurements and the others to hear the difference.
generate-test-tone.diagram1: 20 Hz ← hearing range → 20 kHz · A4 = 440 Hz.

test-microphone.name: How to test your microphone
test-microphone.blurb: Allow the microphone, check the level meter, record five seconds and play it back. Fixes for a silent or clipping mic. Nothing is uploaded.
test-microphone.title: How to test your microphone online
test-microphone.lead: Before a call, a stream or a recording you want to know that your microphone works and sounds right. You will allow access, check the level, record a sample and fix common problems. The sound stays in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
test-microphone.result: A working microphone with speech peaks in a good range, and a short recording that shows how you sound.
test-microphone.note: Plug in the microphone or headset first. Close other apps that use it, such as call apps.
test-microphone.s1t: Know what a good level is
test-microphone.s1b: Levels are in dBFS: 0 is the loudest a recording can hold. Speech peaks between −20 and −6 dBFS are good; near 0 the sound clips and distorts, below −20 it is too quiet.
test-microphone.s2b: Press Start microphone. The browser asks for permission; allow it.
test-microphone.s3b: Speak or clap. The meter, Level, Peak and the waveform should move. The line under the meter says whether the level is good, quiet or too loud.
test-microphone.s4b: Once access is allowed, Input device lists your microphones by name. Pick another one if the meter does not move.
test-microphone.s5b: Press Record 5 s and speak normally. When it stops, a player appears: listen for echo, hum or a muffled sound.
test-microphone.s6b: No movement: check mute switches and the system input volume, and that no other app holds the mic. Too loud: move back or lower the input gain. Blocked: allow the microphone in the site settings.
test-microphone.diagram1: −20 to −6 dBFS good · near 0 clips · below −20 quiet.
test-microphone.diagram2: Start → allow → speak → Record 5 s → play.

use-tally-counter.name: How to use an online tally counter
use-tally-counter.blurb: Count people, laps, stitches or votes with big buttons or the keyboard, keep several named counters and read the total. Counts stay in your browser.
use-tally-counter.title: How to use an online tally counter
use-tally-counter.lead: You need to count something as it happens — visitors at a door, laps, rows of knitting or votes. You will count with buttons or keys, add a counter for each thing and copy the totals. Counts are kept in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
use-tally-counter.result: One or more named counters with their counts and a total, saved in this browser.
use-tally-counter.note: On a phone, keep the screen on while counting. Private windows may forget the counts when closed.
use-tally-counter.s1b: Decide how many things you count at once — for example adults and children, or votes for each option. You will need one counter for each.
use-tally-counter.s2b: One counter, “Counter 1”, starts at 0. Click its name to rename it.
use-tally-counter.s3b: Press + to add and − to subtract. On a keyboard, Space, ↑ or + adds and ↓ or − subtracts on the highlighted counter.
use-tally-counter.s4b: Press Add counter for each extra thing (up to 12). Click a counter to highlight it for the keyboard. The total of all counters appears underneath.
use-tally-counter.s5b: To count in twos or tens, set Step. Tick “Allow negative numbers” only if a count may go below zero, such as a score.
use-tally-counter.s6b: Copy counts puts each name and count on the clipboard. Reset clears one counter; Reset all clears them all.
use-tally-counter.diagram1: + adds · − subtracts · Space ↑ ↓ on the keyboard.

test-webcam.name: How to test your webcam
test-webcam.blurb: Check the preview, the real resolution and frame rate, and take a test photo. Nothing is uploaded.
test-webcam.title: How to test your webcam
test-webcam.lead: You have a video call coming up, or a new webcam, and want to know it works and how good it looks. You will open the camera, read what it really sends and fix the usual problems. The video stays in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
test-webcam.result: A working preview, the camera's real resolution, aspect ratio and frame rate, and a test photo on your device.
test-webcam.note: Video apps may lower the resolution again to save bandwidth; this test shows what the camera itself can send.
test-webcam.s1b: Four things decide how you look on a call: resolution (720p or 1080p), frame rate (30 fps is smooth), focus and light. The test shows the first two as numbers; a photo shows the rest.
test-webcam.s2b: Press Start camera and allow access in the prompt. You see yourself in the preview, mirrored as in a mirror; untick Mirror the preview to see what others see.
test-webcam.s3b: With more than one camera, choose it in the Camera list. Choose 720p or 1080p in Resolution; the panel shows the size you really get, which may be lower if the camera cannot do it.
test-webcam.s4b: Frame rate is measured from the frames actually shown. 30 fps is smooth; 15 fps or less usually means the room is too dark and the camera is exposing longer.
test-webcam.s5t: Fix a black or missing camera
test-webcam.s5b: Close other apps that use the camera, open the privacy shutter or press the camera key, allow camera access for the browser in system settings, and try another USB port.
test-webcam.s6b: Press Take photo to check sharpness and colour, and Save photo to keep it. Face a window or a lamp rather than having it behind you.
test-webcam.diagram2: Black preview: other app · shutter · permission · USB port.

test-gamepad.name: How to test a controller and check stick drift
test-gamepad.blurb: Press every button, read both sticks and spot drift before it costs you a game. Nothing is uploaded.
test-gamepad.title: How to test a controller and check stick drift
test-gamepad.lead: Your character keeps walking on its own, or a button feels dead. You will connect the controller to the browser, test every button and trigger, and read the sticks at rest to see if they drift. Nothing is uploaded.
test-gamepad.result: Every button marked as working or not, trigger travel, both sticks' positions and a drift reading at rest.
test-gamepad.note: Games hide small drift with a dead zone, so 0.05–0.15 may not matter; it tends to grow as a stick wears.
test-gamepad.s1b: Plug it in by USB or pair it by Bluetooth. Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro and most generic pads work in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
test-gamepad.s2t: Open Gamepad tester and press a button
test-gamepad.s2b: Browsers only show a controller after a button press, so press any button. The panel shows its name, layout and how many buttons and axes it has.
test-gamepad.s3b: Each button fills while held and stays outlined once it has worked. Squeeze the triggers slowly: they fill part way, showing their full travel.
test-gamepad.s4b: Move each stick around the edge, then let go. At rest it should read close to 0.00. Above 0.05 is slight drift; 0.15 or more usually shows in games.
test-gamepad.s5b: Press Test vibration. Both motors should rumble for under a second. It needs Chrome or Edge, and some Bluetooth links do not pass it through.
test-gamepad.s6b: For mild drift, raise the dead zone in the game's settings. Strong drift or a dead button usually needs cleaning, a stick module or a repair.
test-gamepad.diagram1: Standard layout: A/✕ B/○ X/□ Y/△, bumpers, triggers, sticks, D-pad.
test-gamepad.diagram2: At rest: under 0.05 fine · 0.05–0.15 slight · 0.15+ drift.

check-dead-pixels.name: How to check a screen for dead pixels
check-dead-pixels.blurb: Show solid colours full screen and find dead, stuck or hot pixels, and tell them from dust.
check-dead-pixels.title: How to check a screen for dead or stuck pixels
check-dead-pixels.lead: You have a new monitor, laptop or phone, or bought one second-hand, and want to be sure every pixel works. You will fill the screen with solid colours and look for dots that do not change. Nothing is uploaded.
check-dead-pixels.result: Any dead, stuck or hot pixels found, and a clear idea whether a spot is a pixel or dust.
check-dead-pixels.note: Check within your return window: many shops and makers accept a screen with a set number of bad pixels only in the first days or weeks.
check-dead-pixels.s1t: Know the three kinds of bad pixel
check-dead-pixels.s1b: A dead pixel stays black (seen best on white), a stuck pixel stays red, green or blue, and a hot pixel stays white (seen best on black).
check-dead-pixels.s2t: Clean the screen and dim the room
check-dead-pixels.s2b: Wipe the screen with a dry microfibre cloth, then open Dead pixel test on cv.cm. Dim lights make small dots easier to see.
check-dead-pixels.s3b: Press Start full screen test. The screen turns black, then white, red, green, blue and gray as you click, press Space or →. ← goes back.
check-dead-pixels.s4b: Look at each colour section by section, close up, including corners and edges. Set Next colour to every 5 seconds if you want your hands free.
check-dead-pixels.s5b: If you see a dot, wipe the spot and look from another angle. Dust moves or blurs; a pixel stays sharp in the same place.
check-dead-pixels.s6b: Note where each pixel is and on which colours it shows. A stuck pixel may recover after some hours of use; a dead pixel rarely does, so use the return or warranty if it bothers you.
check-dead-pixels.diagram1: Dead = black dot · stuck = coloured dot · hot = white dot.
check-dead-pixels.diagram2: Black · white · red · green · blue · gray.

check-refresh-rate.name: How to check your monitor's refresh rate
check-refresh-rate.blurb: Measure the Hz your browser really draws at, and fix a fast screen stuck at 60 Hz.
check-refresh-rate.title: How to check your monitor's refresh rate (Hz)
check-refresh-rate.lead: You bought a 120, 144 or 240 Hz screen and want to be sure it runs that fast. You will measure the rate in the browser, read frame time and skipped frames, and check the usual settings that hold it back. Nothing is uploaded.
check-refresh-rate.result: Your measured refresh rate, the nearest standard rate, the frame time in ms and a count of skipped frames.
check-refresh-rate.note: The browser draws once per screen refresh, so this measures what you actually get, including caps from settings or power saving.
check-refresh-rate.s1b: Refresh rate is how many times a second the screen shows a new image. 60 Hz is a new frame every 16.7 ms, 144 Hz every 6.9 ms, 240 Hz every 4.2 ms.
check-refresh-rate.s2t: Open Refresh rate test on cv.cm
check-refresh-rate.s2b: The test starts by itself. Keep the tab in front and the window on the screen you want to test for a few seconds.
check-refresh-rate.s3b: The big number is the measured rate in Hz, with the nearest standard rate below. Frame time is the median time between frames.
check-refresh-rate.s4b: Spikes in the graph are skipped frames. Watch the moving block at different speeds: at a higher rate it moves in smaller steps and looks smoother.
check-refresh-rate.s5t: Fix a screen stuck at 60 Hz
check-refresh-rate.s5b: Set the rate in system display settings, use a cable and port that carry it (DisplayPort or HDMI 2.0+), turn off battery saver, and plug the laptop in.
check-refresh-rate.s6b: Press Measure again after each change. With two screens, drag the window to the other one and measure there too.
check-refresh-rate.diagram2: Stuck at 60: settings · cable · battery saver · screen.

test-touch-screen.name: How to test a touch screen
test-touch-screen.blurb: Find dead zones, count how many fingers the screen tracks and check pen pressure. Nothing is uploaded.
test-touch-screen.title: How to test a touch screen for dead zones and multi-touch
test-touch-screen.lead: Taps in one part of your screen do nothing, or you want to check a phone or tablet before buying it. You will draw over a grid to find dead zones, count how many fingers the screen tracks and check a pen. Nothing is uploaded.
test-touch-screen.result: A grid showing every part of the screen that responds, the most fingers tracked at once and whether pressure is reported.
test-touch-screen.note: A screen protector, wet fingers or a charger with a poor ground can make touch jumpy; test without them if something looks wrong.
test-touch-screen.s1t: Remove what gets in the way
test-touch-screen.s1b: Take off thick gloves, dry your fingers and, if touch is erratic, unplug the charger. Clean the screen.
test-touch-screen.s2t: Open Touch screen test on cv.cm
test-touch-screen.s2b: The pad shows a grid. Press Full screen to make the pad cover the whole screen so you can reach every edge.
test-touch-screen.s3b: Draw slow lines across the pad, row by row, to the edges and corners. Every cell you touch fills in; cells that stay empty mark a dead zone.
test-touch-screen.s4b: Put down as many fingers as you can at once. Touching now shows the count; Most at once keeps the highest. Each finger draws in its own colour.
test-touch-screen.s5b: Draw with a stylus. Input shows Pen, and Pressure changes as you press harder if the pen reports it.
test-touch-screen.s6b: Press Clear and test again to confirm a dead zone. If the same cells never respond, it is the screen or digitiser, not the app.
test-touch-screen.diagram1: Swipe every row: empty cells = dead zone.
test-touch-screen.diagram2: Phones and tablets: 5–10 fingers · many laptops: 2.

use-scientific-calculator.name: How to use a scientific calculator
use-scientific-calculator.blurb: Get the order, brackets, DEG and RAD, powers, logs and % right, and reuse answers.
use-scientific-calculator.title: How to use a scientific calculator
use-scientific-calculator.lead: You have a sum with brackets, a power or a sine in it, and the answer has to be right. You will type it in the correct order, pick the right angle mode, and reuse results without retyping. It runs in your browser.
use-scientific-calculator.result: A correct result for sums with brackets, powers, roots, logs and trig, with the last 20 kept in your history.
use-scientific-calculator.note: Most wrong answers come from two things: a missing bracket, or the wrong angle mode. Check those two first.
use-scientific-calculator.s1b: The calculator follows standard maths order: brackets first, then powers, then × and ÷, then + and −. So 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20.
use-scientific-calculator.s2t: Open the Scientific calculator on cv.cm
use-scientific-calculator.s2b: Tap the keys or type with your keyboard. The result appears as you type. Enter or = finishes the sum, Esc clears it, and ^ makes a power.
use-scientific-calculator.s3t: Add brackets where the order matters
use-scientific-calculator.s3b: Write (2 + 3) × 4 to get 20. Put the whole top and bottom of a fraction in brackets: (2 + 6) ÷ (1 + 3) is 2. A bracket left open is closed for you at the end of the sum, so check that it closes where you meant. Check the expression usually means an extra ) or a missing number.
use-scientific-calculator.s4t: Choose DEG or RAD before using sin, cos or tan
use-scientific-calculator.s4b: The DEG / RAD button switches between degrees and radians. Angles from a triangle or a protractor are in degrees; formulas with π are usually in radians. sin(30) is 0.5 in DEG and −0.988 in RAD.
use-scientific-calculator.s5b: xʸ makes any power (2^10 is 1024), √ is the square root, x! the factorial. log is base 10 and ln is base e. % only divides by 100: 200 × 10% is 20, but 200 + 10% is 200.1. For a price plus 10%, write 200 × 1.1.
use-scientific-calculator.s6t: Reuse answers and copy the result
use-scientific-calculator.s6b: Ans puts the last answer into the next sum. History keeps your last 20 sums; pick one to use it again. Copy result sends the answer to the clipboard, ready to paste.
use-scientific-calculator.diagram1: Brackets change which part is worked out first.
use-scientific-calculator.diagram2: The same sin(30) gives two answers: check DEG or RAD first.

use-online-notepad.name: How to use an online notepad
use-online-notepad.blurb: Notes that save as you type. Open and download .txt files, and know where the note lives.
use-online-notepad.title: How to use an online notepad
use-online-notepad.lead: You need somewhere to put text right now, with no account or app. You will write a note that saves itself, open or download a text file, and learn the one thing that can lose it. The note stays in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
use-online-notepad.result: A note that survives closing the tab, and a .txt copy on your device whenever you want one.
use-online-notepad.note: The note lives in this browser on this device only. Download it before you clear browser data or change devices.
use-online-notepad.s1t: Know where the note is kept
use-online-notepad.s1b: The note is saved in this browser on this device, not on a server. So it never leaves your device, but it does not follow you to your phone or to another browser.
use-online-notepad.s2t: Open the Online notepad on cv.cm
use-online-notepad.s2b: Start typing. The page saves shortly after you stop and shows the time of the last save. Close the tab and come back: the note is still there.
use-online-notepad.s3t: Set the view for what you are writing
use-online-notepad.s3b: Under View, turn off Wrap long lines for code or logs, so one line stays one line, and turn on Monospace font to line up columns. The counter shows words, characters and lines.
use-online-notepad.s4b: Open file loads a UTF-8 text file up to 1 MB into the note, replacing what is there; Undo brings the old note back for a few seconds. A file in another encoding is refused and your note is unchanged.
use-online-notepad.s5b: Download .txt saves the note as a file on your device. Do this for anything you would be sorry to lose. Copy all puts the whole note on the clipboard to paste into an email or a document.
use-online-notepad.s6t: Clear it, and undo if you change your mind
use-online-notepad.s6b: Clear empties the note, and Undo appears for a few seconds to bring it back. If the page says this browser is not saving notes, you are probably in a private window: download before you close it.
use-online-notepad.diagram1: Saved in this browser only: download a copy to take it elsewhere.
use-online-notepad.diagram2: Wrap on suits writing; wrap off keeps each line of code or logs whole.

preview-markdown.name: How to write and preview Markdown
preview-markdown.blurb: Headings, bold, lists, links, tables and task lists with a live preview, then copy the HTML.
preview-markdown.title: How to write and preview Markdown
preview-markdown.lead: You have a README, a forum post or some notes to format, and want to see the result as you write. You will learn the marks you actually need, check them in a live preview, and take away Markdown or HTML. Nothing is uploaded.
preview-markdown.result: A formatted document you have checked by eye, ready as Markdown, a .md file, HTML you can paste, or an HTML file.
preview-markdown.note: Markdown is plain text, so it opens anywhere. Sites differ on extras such as tables, so check them where you will publish.
preview-markdown.s1b: # and a space make a heading (## and a space a smaller one). **Two stars** make bold and *one star* italic. A line starting with - and a space is a list item, and [text](https://example.com) is a link. Leave a blank line between paragraphs.
preview-markdown.s2b: The Markdown box starts with a short example of every mark, and Show example brings it back at any time. Replace it with your own text and read the result in the Preview box as you go.
preview-markdown.s3b: Separate table cells with | and put a row of dashes under the header; a colon in that row sets the alignment. - [ ] is an open task and - [x] a finished one. Add ~~two tildes~~ for strikethrough.
preview-markdown.s4b: Wrap a word in single backticks for inline code. Put three backticks on a line above and below a block, and the block keeps its line breaks. Tab indents a line; press Esc and then Tab to leave the box.
preview-markdown.s5b: Raw HTML shows as plain text and is never run. Only http, https, mailto, tel and relative links become links, so a link that stays as text has an address the page will not trust.
preview-markdown.s6b: Copy Markdown and Download .md give you the source. Copy HTML and Download HTML give the finished page code. The text also stays in this browser, so you can come back to it.
preview-markdown.diagram1: What you type on the left, what readers see on the right.
preview-markdown.diagram2: A row of dashes makes a table; brackets make a checklist.

make-css-gradient.name: How to make a CSS gradient
make-css-gradient.blurb: Pick linear, radial or conic, set the colours and positions, then copy the CSS or save a PNG.
make-css-gradient.title: How to make a CSS gradient
make-css-gradient.lead: You want a gradient behind a page, a card or a slide, and writing the CSS by trial and error is slow. You will pick a type, place the colours, and copy CSS that is ready to paste, or save an image. It runs in your browser.
make-css-gradient.result: A CSS background rule with a solid fallback colour, or a PNG at 1080p, 1440p, portrait or square size.
make-css-gradient.note: Text over a gradient has to stay readable at both ends. Test the lightest and darkest colours with the text colour you plan to use.
make-css-gradient.s1b: Linear blends in a straight line and suits most backgrounds. Radial spreads out from the centre, like a soft glow. Conic sweeps around a point, like a colour wheel or a pie chart.
make-css-gradient.s2t: Open the CSS gradient generator on cv.cm
make-css-gradient.s2b: Pick the type under Gradient. Press a preset for a starting point or Random for ideas, and the preview updates straight away.
make-css-gradient.s3b: For linear and conic, drag Angle: 0° points up, 90° points right, and 180° points down. For radial, choose Circle or Ellipse instead.
make-css-gradient.s4b: Each colour has a position from 0% to 100%, and you can use up to 6. Add colour inserts one, and × removes it. Close positions make a sharp edge, and far-apart positions make a soft blend.
make-css-gradient.s5b: Copy CSS gives you two lines: a solid colour for very old browsers, then the gradient. Paste them into your element's CSS rule. It works on any block with a size, such as body or a card.
make-css-gradient.s6b: For slides and wallpapers, choose an Image size and press Save PNG. Sizes include 1920 × 1080, 2560 × 1440, 1080 × 1920 for phones and 1080 × 1080 for square posts.
make-css-gradient.diagram1: The three types differ in the path the colours follow.
make-css-gradient.diagram2: Each colour sits at a position on the line, and the CSS lists them in order.

make-fancy-text.name: How to make fancy text
make-fancy-text.blurb: Turn plain letters into bold, script, gothic and circled text you can paste, and know the limits.
make-fancy-text.title: How to make fancy text
make-fancy-text.lead: You want a bio, a username or a heading to stand out where the app gives you no font options. You will convert your text, copy one style and paste it, and learn where it does not work. It runs in your browser.
make-fancy-text.result: Styled text that pastes into social bios, names and posts as ordinary characters, with no font to install.
make-fancy-text.note: These are not fonts. They are separate Unicode symbols that look like letters, which is why they paste anywhere, and also why they have limits.
make-fancy-text.s1t: Know what fancy text really is
make-fancy-text.s1b: Unicode includes sets of symbols that look like bold, script or gothic letters, many first added for maths. Fancy text swaps each letter for one of those symbols, so the style travels with the text.
make-fancy-text.s2t: Open the Fancy text generator on cv.cm
make-fancy-text.s2b: Type in Your text. Every style updates below it as you type, from Bold and Script to Gothic, Circled and Upside down.
make-fancy-text.s3t: Pick a style that stays readable
make-fancy-text.s3b: Bold and Sans bold are the easiest to read. Script and Gothic suit a short name or a few words, not a whole paragraph. Keep the rest of your bio in plain text.
make-fancy-text.s4b: Press Copy beside the style you want and paste it into the app. Check it after saving: an empty box or a question mark means that device has no symbol for that character.
make-fancy-text.s5t: Expect other characters to stay the same
make-fancy-text.s5b: Letter styles change only A–Z, a–z and, in some styles, digits. Chinese, Japanese, Korean and accented letters such as é have no matching symbols, so they stay as typed. Strikethrough and Underline add a line to every character, and Upside down reverses the whole text.
make-fancy-text.s6t: Keep it out of the places where it hurts
make-fancy-text.s6b: Avoid it for anything people need to find or hear. Search may not match 𝐜𝐚𝐤𝐞 with cake, and screen readers may skip the symbols or read out their long names. Leave your real name and key words plain.
make-fancy-text.diagram1: The same word, but different Unicode symbols, not a font.
make-fancy-text.diagram2: Letter styles change only A–Z, a–z and some digits; everything else stays as typed.

flip-coin.name: How to flip a coin online
flip-coin.blurb: Settle it fairly, flip up to 1,000 coins, and read streaks without being fooled by them.
flip-coin.title: How to flip a coin online
flip-coin.lead: Two people need a fair decision, or a class wants to see how chance behaves, and nobody has a coin. You will agree the call, flip one coin or up to 1,000, and read the totals and streaks. It runs in your browser.
flip-coin.result: A fair heads or tails, or a batch of up to 1,000 flips with totals, percentages and streaks, and a summary you can copy.
flip-coin.note: Each coin uses one secure random bit from your browser, so heads and tails are equally likely and earlier flips do not matter.
flip-coin.s1b: Say who has heads and what each side means before you flip, and that one flip decides. A decision made in advance is what makes the flip fair to everyone.
flip-coin.s2b: Tap the coin or press Flip. Space and Enter also flip it. The face shown when it stops is the result.
flip-coin.s3b: Choose 10, 100 or 1,000 under Coins per flip. All of them land together and the page shows how many came up heads and tails, which is handy for a probability lesson.
flip-coin.s4b: Results add up every flip since the last Reset, so press Reset first to read one batch on its own. Expect close to half each, not exactly half: in 100 coins, anything from 40 to 60 heads happens about 96% of the time.
flip-coin.s5t: Do not read meaning into streaks
flip-coin.s5b: Longest streak and Current streak show runs of the same face. They look surprising but are normal. After five heads in a row, the next coin is still 50% heads.
flip-coin.s6b: Copy results gives you a line with the totals to paste in a chat or a report. Last 100 coins shows the recent faces in order. Reset starts a new count.
flip-coin.diagram1: Every flip is an even split: one bit, two equal faces.
flip-coin.diagram2: The coin has no memory: after any run, the next flip is still 50%.

tune-guitar.name: How to tune a guitar
tune-guitar.blurb: Tune E A D G B E with your microphone, read flat and sharp, and always tune up to the note.
tune-guitar.title: How to tune a guitar
tune-guitar.lead: Your guitar sounds off, or it is your first time tuning. You will set up the tuner, play one string at a time, and turn the pegs until each is within ±5 cents. It listens through your microphone, and nothing is recorded or uploaded.
tune-guitar.result: All six strings in standard tuning (E A D G B E), each within ±5 cents of its note.
tune-guitar.note: New strings and big temperature changes make a guitar drift, so a second pass is normal, and new strings may need several.
tune-guitar.s1b: Standard tuning from the thickest string to the thinnest is E A D G B E. The thickest is low E (about 82 Hz), and the thinnest is high E (about 330 Hz), two octaves higher.
tune-guitar.s2t: Open the Guitar tuner on cv.cm
tune-guitar.s2b: Press Start tuner and allow the microphone when the browser asks. Instrument defaults to standard guitar. Move to a quiet room and hold the guitar close to the microphone.
tune-guitar.s3t: Play one string and read the meter
tune-guitar.s3b: Leave Auto on, then pluck one string and let it ring. The page shows the closest string's note and how many cents off it is. In tune means within ±5 cents; a cent is one hundredth of a semitone.
tune-guitar.s4t: Turn the peg the right way
tune-guitar.s4b: Flat means too low, so tighten the string. Sharp means too high, so loosen it. Turn slowly and pluck again, because a small turn moves the pitch quickly, especially on the thin strings.
tune-guitar.s5b: If a string is sharp, loosen it below the note and come back up. The string then holds its pitch better, because no slack is left at the peg. Do the same for all six strings.
tune-guitar.s6t: Check again, or change the tuning
tune-guitar.s6b: Pulling one string slightly changes the others, so go through them all again. If Auto jumps between strings, tap one to lock onto it. Instrument also has drop D, DADGAD, open G, bass, ukulele, violin and cello.
tune-guitar.diagram1: Thickest to thinnest: E A D G B E, each with its target pitch.
tune-guitar.diagram2: Left of centre is flat, right of centre is sharp, and ±5 cents counts as in tune.

find-factors.name: How to find the factors of a number
find-factors.blurb: Get all factors, pairs and the prime factorization, and see how the factor count is worked out.
find-factors.title: How to find the factors of a number
find-factors.lead: You need the factors of a number for homework, for simplifying, or to check whether it is prime. You will find them by hand for a small number, then read the full answer for any whole number up to 18 digits. It runs in your browser with exact maths.
find-factors.result: Whether the number is prime, its prime factorization, the number and sum of its factors, and every factor pair for numbers with up to 2,000 factors.
find-factors.note: A factor divides a number with nothing left over. Each factor comes with a partner, so you only need to test up to the square root.
find-factors.s1t: Find the prime factors by hand
find-factors.s1b: Keep dividing by the smallest prime that fits. 360 ÷ 2 = 180, ÷ 2 = 90, ÷ 2 = 45, ÷ 3 = 15, ÷ 3 = 5, and 5 is prime. So 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5.
find-factors.s2t: Open the Factor calculator on cv.cm
find-factors.s2b: Type a whole number or tap an example such as 97 or 1001. You can group digits in threes, as in 1,234,567. The answer updates as you type.
find-factors.s3b: The first line says whether the number is prime, and the table lists the Previous prime and Next prime. 97 is prime; 1001 is not, as 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13. 1 is neither, as it has only one factor.
find-factors.s4b: Prime factorization gives the compact form, and Written out repeats every prime: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5. Every whole number above 1 has exactly one such list of primes.
find-factors.s5b: Factor pairs are two numbers that multiply to give yours: 36 is 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9 and 6 × 6. They are also every whole-number rectangle of that area, which is useful for layouts and seating.
find-factors.s6b: Add 1 to each exponent and multiply. 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5¹ has 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 factors, which is the Number of divisors shown. All factors lists them, showing the first 1,000 if there are more.
find-factors.diagram1: Split until every branch ends in a prime: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5.
find-factors.diagram2: Each factor has a partner, and the pairs stop at the square root.

find-lcm-gcf.name: How to find the LCM and GCF
find-lcm-gcf.blurb: Work out the least common multiple and greatest common factor, and know which one you need.
find-lcm-gcf.title: How to find the LCM and GCF
find-lcm-gcf.lead: You are adding fractions, simplifying one, or working out when two schedules line up. You will learn which of the two you need, find it by hand with prime factors, and check it with exact maths in your browser.
find-lcm-gcf.result: The GCF and LCM of 2 to 20 whole numbers, with the prime factors and, for two numbers, Euclid's steps.
find-lcm-gcf.note: GCF is also called GCD or HCF, and they all mean the same thing. The LCM of two fractions' denominators is their lowest common denominator.
find-lcm-gcf.s1b: Use the GCF to split into equal groups or simplify a fraction: 12/18 divided by 6 is 2/3. Use the LCM to find when things line up or to add fractions: buses every 12 and 18 minutes meet every 36 minutes.
find-lcm-gcf.s2t: Open the LCM and GCF calculator on cv.cm
find-lcm-gcf.s2b: Type 2 to 20 whole numbers separated by commas or spaces, or tap an example such as 8, 12. Do not use thousands separators, as a comma always starts a new number.
find-lcm-gcf.s3b: Write each as primes: 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3². GCF takes each shared prime at its lowest power, 2 × 3 = 6. LCM takes every prime at its highest power, 2² × 3² = 36.
find-lcm-gcf.s4t: Use Euclid's algorithm for big numbers
find-lcm-gcf.s4b: Divide the larger by the smaller and keep the remainder, then repeat with the divisor and the remainder. 18 = 1 × 12 + 6, and 12 = 2 × 6 + 0. The last divisor, 6, is the GCF. The page shows these steps for two numbers.
find-lcm-gcf.s5b: For two numbers, LCM × GCF equals the two numbers multiplied: 36 × 6 = 12 × 18 = 216. That lets you get the LCM straight from the GCF. This shortcut does not work for three or more numbers.
find-lcm-gcf.s6t: Read the result and copy it
find-lcm-gcf.s6b: The page lists both results and the prime factors of each number. Coprime: Yes means the GCF is 1, so no prime divides all of them. For two numbers, the LCM is then their product; with three or more it can be smaller (6, 10, 15 has an LCM of 30). Copy result sends the answer to your clipboard.
find-lcm-gcf.diagram1: Shared primes make the GCF; all the primes together make the LCM.
find-lcm-gcf.diagram2: Each line divides by the last remainder until nothing is left.

use-emulator.name: How to use an emulator
use-emulator.blurb: Open a ROM in your browser, check the console, learn the keys and save your game.
use-emulator.title: How to use an emulator to play ROMs
use-emulator.lead: You have a ROM file and want to play it without installing anything. You will open it in the browser, check the console, learn the keys and save your progress. The file stays on your device.
use-emulator.result: Your game running in a browser tab, with its keys in front of you and a save state on your device.
use-emulator.note: Use ROMs you have the right to use, such as homebrew released by its author. cv.cm does not provide commercial ROMs.
use-emulator.s1t: Find a ROM you can use
use-emulator.s1b: A ROM is a copy of a game cartridge in one file. This tool opens FC / NES, SFC / SNES, Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance and Mega Drive / Genesis games. cv.cm's Games column has free homebrew if you have no file.
use-emulator.s2t: Open the ROM emulator on cv.cm
use-emulator.s2b: Press Choose ROM and pick a .nes, .sfc, .smc, .gb, .gbc, .gba, .md, .gen, .smd, .bin or .zip file. It is read in this tab and not sent anywhere. The first start also downloads the emulator, so give it a moment.
use-emulator.s3b: The line under the game says which console was detected. If the file does not say, or the game looks wrong, choose one under Console and the game starts again on it. Game Boy and Game Boy Color share one emulator core, so switching between those two does not restart the game.
use-emulator.s4b: The keys for that console appear under the game. On most consoles the arrow keys move, Z is A, X is B, V is Select and Enter is Start. On a phone, use the on-screen pad. A Bluetooth gamepad works too.
use-emulator.s5b: Move the pointer over the game to show the toolbar. On a phone, tap the three-line icon at the top right. The floppy disk icon saves a state and downloads it as a .state file. The folder icon loads one. Keep the file: it brings you back to this exact spot after you close the tab.
use-emulator.s6t: Fix a game that will not start
use-emulator.s6b: A black screen usually means the wrong console, so try another under Console. A zip must hold a ROM directly, not another zip. Files over 64 MB are refused, because they are too big for these consoles, and disc games are not supported.
use-emulator.diagram1: Each file type and the console it opens on.
use-emulator.diagram2: The keyboard keys for most consoles, and what SFC adds.

open-swf-file.name: How to open SWF files
open-swf-file.blurb: Open a .swf file with no plugin, turn on the sound, and see why some files stop loading.
open-swf-file.title: How to open SWF files without Flash
open-swf-file.lead: You have a .swf file and Flash Player no longer works. You will open it in a browser tab with Ruffle, turn on the sound, play it, and see what to do when it stops loading. The file stays on your device.
open-swf-file.result: Your SWF running in a browser tab, with sound, and no plugin installed.
open-swf-file.note: Do not install old Flash Player downloads from other sites. Adobe stopped supporting Flash Player and recommends uninstalling it.
open-swf-file.s1b: A SWF is a Flash file: a game, animation or small app. Adobe ended Flash Player support on December 31, 2020 and blocked Flash content from January 12, 2021, so browsers no longer run these files by themselves.
open-swf-file.s2t: Open the Flash player on cv.cm
open-swf-file.s2b: Press Choose SWF and pick your .swf file. It stays in this tab and is not sent to a server. The first start also downloads Ruffle, an open-source Flash emulator, which can take a few seconds.
open-swf-file.s3b: Browsers may block audio that plays by itself. If you hear nothing, click the picture once.
open-swf-file.s4b: Most Flash files use the left mouse button. A tap on a phone counts as a click. Arrow keys work when the game expects a keyboard, so a computer is easier for those games.
open-swf-file.s5t: See why a file stops loading
open-swf-file.s5b: This page only runs a file that can start on its own, and it blocks network access. A game that loads more SWFs or XML, or only runs on its old website, stops on its loader.
open-swf-file.s6t: Try something else if it fails
open-swf-file.s6b: Ruffle runs most older ActionScript 1 and 2 files, but its ActionScript 3 support is incomplete, so some newer games fail or misbehave. Choose SWF again to open another file, or play the free titles under Flash games.
open-swf-file.diagram1: How mouse, touch and keyboard work in a Flash file.
open-swf-file.diagram2: A SWF that starts alone runs. One that needs other files or its old website stops.

calculate-mortgage.name: How to calculate a mortgage payment
calculate-mortgage.blurb: Monthly payment, total interest and the balance each year, from four numbers.
calculate-mortgage.title: How to calculate a mortgage payment
calculate-mortgage.lead: Before you talk to a bank, you want to know what a home will cost each month and in total. You will turn the price, down payment, rate and term into a monthly payment and a year-by-year schedule. It runs in your browser.
calculate-mortgage.result: The monthly payment, the total interest, and how much of the loan is left after each year.
calculate-mortgage.note: The result is principal and interest only. Property tax, home insurance and mortgage insurance come on top.
calculate-mortgage.s1b: You need the home price, the down payment as a percentage, the yearly interest rate and the term in years. The loan is the price minus the down payment: 400,000 with 20% down is a 320,000 loan.
calculate-mortgage.s2t: Open the Mortgage calculator on cv.cm
calculate-mortgage.s2b: Type the four numbers into Home price, Down payment (%), Interest rate (% per year) and Term (years). The result updates as you type.
calculate-mortgage.s3t: Read the monthly payment and total interest
calculate-mortgage.s3b: With Equal payments, 320,000 at 6.5% for 30 years is 2,022.62 a month. Over 360 payments that is 408,142 in interest, more than the loan itself. A lower rate or a shorter term cuts that figure fast.
calculate-mortgage.s4t: Compare Equal payments with Equal principal
calculate-mortgage.s4b: Switch Repayment to Equal principal. Each month repays the same part of the loan plus that month's interest, so the same loan starts at 2,622.22, falls by 4.81 every month to 893.70, and costs 312,867 in interest. It saves money but needs a higher payment at the start.
calculate-mortgage.s5b: Each row is one year: how much went to principal, how much to interest, and the balance left. With equal payments, year 1 is mostly interest (20,695 interest, 3,577 principal); by the last year it is almost all principal.
calculate-mortgage.s6t: Try other numbers and copy the result
calculate-mortgage.s6b: Change one number at a time, such as 10 more years or 1% less interest, to see what it really changes. Copy result copies the summary for your notes or a message.
calculate-mortgage.diagram1: Each year's payments: early years go mostly to interest, later years mostly to the loan.
calculate-mortgage.diagram2: Equal payments stay flat; equal principal starts higher and falls every month.

solve-quadratic.name: How to solve a quadratic equation
solve-quadratic.blurb: Find a, b and c, check the discriminant, and use the quadratic formula.
solve-quadratic.title: How to solve a quadratic equation
solve-quadratic.lead: You have an equation with an x² in it and need the values of x. You will put it in standard form, see how many answers it has, work them out with the quadratic formula, and check them on a graph. A solver checks each step in your browser.
solve-quadratic.result: The roots of the equation, exact and as decimals, with the working and a graph.
solve-quadratic.note: Most mistakes are sign mistakes. Keep the minus sign with its number when you read off b and c.
solve-quadratic.s1t: Put the equation in standard form
solve-quadratic.s1b: Move every term to one side so it reads ax² + bx + c = 0. For x² = 3x − 2, subtract 3x and add 2: x² − 3x + 2 = 0. Now a = 1, b = −3 and c = 2.
solve-quadratic.s2t: Open the Quadratic equation solver on cv.cm
solve-quadratic.s2b: Type a, b and c into their boxes. Leave b or c empty if that term is missing: x² − 4 = 0 has a = 1, b = 0, c = −4. a cannot be 0, or it is not quadratic.
solve-quadratic.s3b: Δ = b² − 4ac decides the answer. For x² − 3x + 2: Δ = 9 − 8 = 1. Positive means two real roots, 0 means one repeated root, negative means no real roots (two complex ones).
solve-quadratic.s4b: x = (−b ± √Δ) ÷ 2a. Here x = (3 ± 1) ÷ 2, so x = 1 or x = 2. Working shows the same steps with your numbers, so you can follow or copy them.
solve-quadratic.s5t: Read exact roots and the factored form
solve-quadratic.s5b: When a, b and c are whole numbers, the solver keeps exact answers: x² − 2x − 1 = 0 gives 1 ± √2 (about −0.414 and 2.414). Rational roots also give the factored form, such as (x − 1)(x − 2) = 0.
solve-quadratic.s6b: The roots are where the parabola crosses the x-axis, marked with circles; the filled dot is the vertex. If the curve never reaches the axis, the roots are complex. Copy result copies everything as text.
solve-quadratic.diagram1: The sign of the discriminant shows how often the parabola meets the x-axis.
solve-quadratic.diagram2: The quadratic formula worked through for x² − 3x + 2 = 0.

make-random-teams.name: How to make random teams
make-random-teams.blurb: Split names into teams of fair size, then share the result.
make-random-teams.title: How to make random teams
make-random-teams.lead: You need to split a class, a club or a group of players into teams, and everyone should see it was fair. You will paste the names, choose how many teams or how many per team, and draw teams that are random and even. It runs in your browser.
make-random-teams.result: Random teams whose sizes differ by at most one, ready to copy and share.
make-random-teams.note: Agree on the team count before you press Generate teams. Drawing again until you like the result is no longer random.
make-random-teams.s1b: Put one name per line, or separate names with commas. A list copied from a spreadsheet column works as it is. If two people share a name, add an initial so you can tell them apart.
make-random-teams.s2t: Open the Random team generator on cv.cm
make-random-teams.s2b: Paste the names into the box. The line under it counts the names, so you can check nobody is missing.
make-random-teams.s3b: Pick Number of teams if you know how many teams you need, or People per team if you know the size. Type the number. The line under the list shows the result, such as 12 names → 3 teams of 4.
make-random-teams.s4t: Know how uneven numbers are handled
make-random-teams.s4b: Names are dealt round-robin, so sizes never differ by more than one: 10 names into 3 teams gives 4, 3 and 3, and which team gets the extra person is random. People per team rounds the number of teams up and spreads everyone evenly: 12 names in teams of 5 makes 3 teams of 4.
make-random-teams.s5b: Press Generate teams. The shuffle uses your browser's cryptographic random numbers, so every split is equally likely. Press it again for a completely new draw.
make-random-teams.s6b: Copy teams copies every team as text, one line per team, ready for a chat or a board. Nothing is saved, so copy the result before you close the tab.
make-random-teams.diagram1: Shuffled names are dealt one by one, so the sizes stay even.
make-random-teams.diagram2: Number of teams and People per team can give the same split.

check-screen-resolution.name: How to check your screen resolution
check-screen-resolution.blurb: Real pixels, CSS pixels, scaling and the browser viewport, explained.
check-screen-resolution.title: How to check your screen resolution
check-screen-resolution.lead: A game, a video setting or a support form asks for your screen resolution, and the numbers you find do not agree. You will find the real resolution, see why scaling changes it, and read the size of your browser window. It works on any computer, tablet or phone.
check-screen-resolution.result: Your screen resolution in real pixels, your display scaling, and the size of the page area in your browser.
check-screen-resolution.note: Browser zoom changes the pixel ratio too. Press Ctrl + 0 (Cmd + 0 on a Mac) to reset zoom to 100% first.
check-screen-resolution.s1b: Zooming a page in or out changes what the browser reports. Press Ctrl + 0, or Cmd + 0 on a Mac, so zoom is 100%. On a phone, pinch back to normal size.
check-screen-resolution.s2b: The large number is your screen resolution in real pixels, such as 1920 × 1080. If it has a common name, like Full HD (1080p) or 4K UHD, that appears in the first row.
check-screen-resolution.s3b: Windows at 125% and Retina screens make text larger by using more real pixels per CSS pixel. Device pixel ratio says how many: a 1920 × 1080 screen at 125% shows 1536 × 864 CSS pixels and a ratio of 1.25.
check-screen-resolution.s4b: Browser viewport is the part of the window that shows the page, in CSS pixels. Resize the window and it changes at once. Web designers use this size for responsive layouts.
check-screen-resolution.s5b: Available screen leaves out the taskbar or Dock. Aspect ratio gives the shape, such as 16:9 or 16:10; Orientation and Colour depth complete the picture. Turn a phone and the values follow.
check-screen-resolution.s6b: Copy details copies every row as text. Paste it into a bug report or support chat so the other side sees exactly what your browser sees.
check-screen-resolution.diagram1: With 125% scaling, 1920 × 1080 real pixels are reported as 1536 × 864 CSS pixels.
check-screen-resolution.diagram2: The screen, the space left by the taskbar, and the viewport inside the browser.

set-online-alarm.name: How to set an online alarm
set-online-alarm.blurb: Set an alarm in the browser, check the sound, and snooze or stop it.
set-online-alarm.title: How to set an online alarm
set-online-alarm.lead: You need an alarm on your computer: for a nap, a meeting or the end of a study session, without installing an app. You will set the time and sound, make sure it can really ring, and snooze or stop it. It runs in your browser tab.
set-online-alarm.result: An alarm that rings at the time you set, with a label you can read from across the room.
set-online-alarm.note: The alarm lives in the tab. Closing the tab, sleep mode or a locked phone can stop it, so keep the tab open and the device awake.
set-online-alarm.s1t: Open the Online alarm clock on cv.cm
set-online-alarm.s1b: The large clock shows the current time on this device. The alarm uses the same clock, so check it is right.
set-online-alarm.s2t: Pick the time, label and sound
set-online-alarm.s2b: Set Alarm time. Add a Label such as Meeting or Take a break; it shows when the alarm rings and in the tab title. Choose a Sound: Beep, Chime, Bell or Digital.
set-online-alarm.s3b: Press Test sound to hear the alarm and set the volume. If you hear nothing, check the system volume, the browser tab is not muted, and a phone is not in silent mode.
set-online-alarm.s4b: Press Set alarm. The page shows when it will ring and a countdown, such as rings in 7 h 30 min. A time earlier than now means tomorrow: set 07:00 at 23:30 and it rings the next morning.
set-online-alarm.s5b: You can switch to other tabs: the sound is queued in the browser's audio engine, so it still rings on time. Do not close the tab, and make sure the computer will not sleep before the alarm time; check its power settings. While this tab is showing, the page also keeps the screen on where the browser allows it.
set-online-alarm.s6b: When it rings, press Stop, or Snooze 5 min or Snooze 10 min to ring again later. If nobody answers, it stops by itself after 10 minutes. Press Cancel alarm to remove it before it rings.
set-online-alarm.diagram1: A time earlier than now rings tomorrow; the page shows how long is left.
set-online-alarm.diagram2: What keeps the alarm working and what stops it.

play-white-noise.name: How to use white noise
play-white-noise.blurb: Pick a noise colour, set a safe volume and a sleep timer.
play-white-noise.title: How to use white noise for sleep and focus
play-white-noise.lead: A steady noise covers sudden sounds such as traffic, neighbours or a snoring partner, which helps many people fall asleep or concentrate. You will pick a noise colour, set a gentle volume, add a sleep timer and keep it playing. It is generated in your browser tab.
play-white-noise.result: A steady, comfortable sound that masks the noises around you and stops by itself when you are asleep.
play-white-noise.note: Noise masks sound; it does not treat insomnia or tinnitus. Keep the level low, especially for babies, and ask a doctor about ongoing sleep or hearing problems.
play-white-noise.s1t: Open the White noise generator on cv.cm
play-white-noise.s1b: Use headphones or a speaker you can place across the room. A phone speaker on the pillow is louder than it sounds.
play-white-noise.s2b: In Noise colour, pick White noise (bright hiss), Pink noise (rain), Brown noise (deep rumble) or Green noise (mid hum). Many people find pink or brown noise easier to sleep with than white.
play-white-noise.s3b: Set Volume low and press Play. Raise it only until the sounds you want to cover fade into the background. It should be quieter than a normal conversation.
play-white-noise.s4b: Pick a Sleep timer such as 30 minutes or 1 h, or leave Off (play until stopped). The sound fades out over the last 30 seconds, so the end does not wake you.
play-white-noise.s5b: You can switch to other tabs or lock the screen on a computer; the sound keeps going. On phones, keep the browser open, since some phones pause web audio when the screen locks.
play-white-noise.s6b: Change the colour or volume while it plays; the switch crossfades smoothly. Press Stop to end it.
play-white-noise.diagram1: How the energy of each noise colour spreads from low to high frequencies.
play-white-noise.diagram2: The sleep timer plays at full level, then fades out over the last 30 seconds.

measure-decibels.name: How to measure decibels
measure-decibels.blurb: Measure noise in dB(A) with your microphone and calibrate it.
measure-decibels.title: How to measure decibels with your phone or laptop
measure-decibels.lead: You want to know how loud a room, a machine or a neighbour really is. You will start the meter, read the level and the average, calibrate it if you have a reference, and compare the result with safe limits. It uses your device's microphone in the browser tab.
measure-decibels.result: A reading in dB(A) with the minimum, maximum and average over the time you measured, ready to compare with noise limits.
measure-decibels.note: A phone or laptop microphone gives an estimate, not a legal measurement. For a complaint or a workplace check, use a certified sound level meter.
measure-decibels.s1t: Open the Decibel meter on cv.cm
measure-decibels.s1b: Leave Frequency weighting on A (like human hearing), which is what noise rules use, and Response on Fast (125 ms). Choose Slow (1 s) for a steadier number.
measure-decibels.s2b: Press Start and allow the microphone. Keep the device still, about 1 m from the source, with the microphone pointing at it and nothing covering it.
measure-decibels.s3b: The big number is the current level in dB(A), with a band such as Quiet or Loud. The graph shows the last 60 seconds; the dashed line is 85 dB.
measure-decibels.s4b: Let it run for at least a minute. Average (Leq) is the energy average, which is how noise limits are written; Max catches the peaks. Press Reset min/max to start a new measurement.
measure-decibels.s5b: Place a real sound level meter next to the device and play a steady sound. Change Calibration (dB) until both show the same number. Without a meter, check that a quiet room reads about 30–40 dB.
measure-decibels.s6b: Long exposure above 85 dB(A) can damage hearing. NIOSH allows 8 hours at 85 dB(A) and half the time for each extra 3 dB. For sleep, the WHO advises keeping night noise outside the bedroom below about 40 dB.
measure-decibels.diagram1: Typical sound levels from breathing to a siren.
measure-decibels.diagram2: Safe listening time halves for every 3 dB above 85 dB(A).

record-voice-online.name: How to record your voice online
record-voice-online.blurb: Record from the microphone, play back and download.
record-voice-online.title: How to record your voice online
record-voice-online.lead: You need a quick voice memo, a voice-over or a song idea without installing an app. You will choose the microphone, check the level, record with pauses, listen back and download the file. Everything happens in your browser tab.
record-voice-online.result: An audio file on your device: WebM or M4A straight from the browser, or a WAV that opens in any editor.
record-voice-online.note: Recordings live only in the tab until you download them. Reloading or closing the page deletes them, so download each take you want to keep.
record-voice-online.s1t: Open the Voice recorder on cv.cm
record-voice-online.s1b: Plug in a headset or USB microphone first if you have one. It usually sounds better than a laptop's built-in microphone.
record-voice-online.s2b: Keep Voice cleanup (noise and echo reduction) on for speech. Turn it off for music, so instruments are not treated as noise. The Microphone list fills in after the first recording.
record-voice-online.s3b: Press Record and allow the microphone. Speak at your normal volume and watch the Input level bar: it should move to the middle on loud words without staying full.
record-voice-online.s4b: The timer shows the length. Press Pause for a break and Resume to carry on in the same file. Press Stop recording when you are done.
record-voice-online.s5b: The take appears under Recordings with its name, length and size. Play it to check it before you download.
record-voice-online.s6b: Press Download WEBM or Download M4A (depending on the browser) for the original small file, or Download WAV for uncompressed audio. Press Delete to remove a take.
record-voice-online.diagram1: From the microphone to a file on your device: nothing leaves the tab.
record-voice-online.diagram2: The original file is small; WAV is larger but opens everywhere.

record-screen-online.name: How to record your screen online
record-screen-online.blurb: Record a screen, window or tab with sound and save the video.
record-screen-online.title: How to record your screen online
record-screen-online.lead: You want to record a tutorial, a bug, a presentation or a video call without installing software. You will pick the format and sound, choose what to share, record and download the video. It runs in your browser on a computer.
record-screen-online.result: An MP4 or WebM video on your computer, with tab or system sound and your voice if you chose them, and no watermark.
record-screen-online.note: Close private tabs and turn off notifications before you share the entire screen: everything visible is recorded. Phones and tablets cannot record the screen from a web page.
record-screen-online.s1t: Open the Screen recorder on cv.cm
record-screen-online.s1b: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. Close windows you do not want in the video.
record-screen-online.s2b: Leave Format on Auto (MP4 if possible) for the file that plays most widely. Quality Standard (4 Mbps) suits most screens; High (8 Mbps) keeps fast motion and small text sharper.
record-screen-online.s3b: Tick System or tab audio to record the sound of what you share, and Microphone to add your voice. Sharing a browser tab is the most reliable way to get its sound.
record-screen-online.s4b: Press Start recording. The browser asks what to share: Entire screen, Window or a Tab. For a tab's sound, keep its audio option on, then press Share.
record-screen-online.s5b: The timer runs while you record. Press Pause and Resume to skip parts. Press Stop recording, or the browser's Stop sharing bar, when you are done.
record-screen-online.s6b: Play the video under the timer, then press Download MP4 or Download WEBM. Press Discard to throw it away and record again.
record-screen-online.diagram1: What each sharing choice records, and where tab sound comes from.
record-screen-online.diagram2: Tab or system sound and the microphone are mixed into one audio track.

solve-triangle.name: How to solve a triangle
solve-triangle.blurb: Find every side, angle and the area from three values.
solve-triangle.title: How to solve a triangle
solve-triangle.lead: You know some sides or angles of a triangle, from homework, a roof, a ramp or a map, and need the rest. You will label the triangle, choose which values you know, let the right rule do the work and check the answer. The calculator shows every step.
solve-triangle.result: All three sides and angles, the area, the perimeter and the heights, with the working and a scaled drawing.
solve-triangle.note: Use the same unit for every side, and degrees for angles. The area comes out in that unit squared.
solve-triangle.s1t: Open the Triangle calculator on cv.cm
solve-triangle.s1b: Sketch the triangle and name its corners A, B and C. Side a is opposite corner A, side b opposite B and side c opposite C.
solve-triangle.s2b: If one angle is 90°, call it C and tick Right triangle (C = 90°). Then c is the hypotenuse and two values are enough: two sides use Pythagoras, a² + b² = c².
solve-triangle.s3b: For any other triangle, enter three values with at least one side: three sides (SSS), two sides and the angle between them (SAS), or two angles and a side (ASA, AAS). Three angles alone fix the shape but not the size.
solve-triangle.s4b: With sides only or an angle between two sides, the law of cosines finds the missing piece: c² = a² + b² − 2ab · cos C. With a side and its opposite angle, the law of sines does: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C.
solve-triangle.s5b: Two sides and an angle that is not between them (SSA) can make two triangles, one acute and one obtuse. The calculator shows Triangle 1 and Triangle 2; pick the one that matches your sketch.
solve-triangle.s6b: Area = ½ · b · c · sin A. Check that the angles add to 180° and that the longest side faces the largest angle. Copy result copies the values and the working.
solve-triangle.diagram1: Each side is named after the angle opposite it; c is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
solve-triangle.diagram2: Two sides and a non-included angle can close in two places.

make-gif.name: How to make a GIF
make-gif.blurb: Animated GIF from photos or a short video clip.
make-gif.title: How to make a GIF from pictures or a video
make-gif.lead: A GIF plays in chats, slides, emails and web pages without a player. You will gather the frames, set their timing, choose a size and repeat, keep the file small and download it. The GIF maker does it in the browser, with no watermark.
make-gif.result: An animated GIF that loops (or plays once) at the speed you chose, ready to send or embed.
make-gif.note: GIF holds at most 256 colours per frame and no sound. For long or detailed clips a short MP4 is often smaller.
make-gif.s1t: Open the GIF maker on cv.cm
make-gif.s1b: Collect the frames: two or more pictures of the same shape, or one short video. Phone photos, screenshots and drawings all work.
make-gif.s2t: Add the frames and set the order
make-gif.s2b: Drop the pictures; each one is a frame and they play top to bottom. Use the arrows to reorder and × to remove. For a video, drop the file and set Start and End in seconds.
make-gif.s3b: For pictures, Delay per frame sets how long each one shows: 500 ms is two frames a second, 100 ms looks like motion. For a video, 10 frames per second is smooth enough for most clips.
make-gif.s4b: Pick a width; the height follows the first frame's shape. Pictures of other shapes can fit inside on the background colour or fill the frame. Choose Loop forever, Play once or Play 3 times.
make-gif.s5b: File size grows with width × height × frames. Halving the width makes the file about four times smaller. Fewer colours and dithering off help flat graphics; keep dithering on for photos.
make-gif.s6b: Press Make GIF. The finished GIF plays below with its size in pixels and bytes. Check it, then Download GIF. Change any setting and make it again if it is too big or too fast.
make-gif.diagram1: Each frame shows for its delay; the loop starts again after the last.
make-gif.diagram2: Width, frame count and colours decide the file size.

split-image.name: How to split an image into a grid
split-image.blurb: Cut one picture into tiles for an Instagram grid or carousel.
split-image.title: How to split an image into a grid for Instagram
split-image.lead: One big picture spread over several posts makes a profile look like a single poster, and a wide photo cut into slides makes a carousel you swipe through. You will choose the grid, crop the tiles to the right shape, split, download and post in the right order.
split-image.result: Equal tiles named by row and column, in a ZIP or one by one, numbered in the order to post them.
split-image.note: Instagram's profile grid has shown every post as a 3:4 thumbnail since 2025. Square tiles lose a little at the left and right there, so the seams show; 3:4 tiles fill each cell exactly. Carousel slides can stay square.
split-image.s1t: Open the Image splitter on cv.cm
split-image.s1b: Pick a sharp picture with the subject near the middle. For a 3 × 3 grid of 1080 × 1440 px tiles, start from a picture at least 3240 × 4320 px.
split-image.s2b: Use 3 × 3 for a nine-post profile block, 1 × 3 carousel for a swipeable panorama, or set rows and columns up to 20 each. The grid is drawn on the picture at once.
split-image.s3b: Use Portrait 3:4 for the profile grid (the 3 × 3 preset already does) and Square 1:1 for carousel slides. The largest grid of that shape that fits is kept in the centre and the dimmed edges are trimmed. Whole picture keeps everything.
split-image.s4b: Press Split. Tiles appear below; tap one to save it, or Download ZIP for all. Files are named photo-r1-c1, photo-r1-c2 and so on, so they sort in reading order.
split-image.s5b: The newest post goes top left, so post the last tile (bottom right) first and the first tile last. Tick Show posting order to number the tiles 1, 2, 3 in the order you post them.
split-image.s6b: For a panorama, select all the slides in one post, in reading order (left to right). People swipe through them as one continuous picture.
split-image.diagram1: A 3 × 3 grid of 3:4 tiles, cut from the centre of the picture.
split-image.diagram2: Post the last tile first: it ends up bottom right.

calculate-area.name: How to calculate area
calculate-area.blurb: Area formulas for rectangles, triangles, circles and more.
calculate-area.title: How to calculate area
calculate-area.lead: Area tells you how much flooring, paint, turf or fabric you need, or how big a plot is. You will measure, pick the formula for the shape, keep one unit, convert the answer, and split odd shapes into simple ones.
calculate-area.result: The area of the shape in square units, its perimeter where it is fixed, and the same area in m², ft², acres or hectares.
calculate-area.note: Area is always in a unit squared: metres give m², feet give ft². Never mix units in one calculation.
calculate-area.s1t: Open the Area calculator on cv.cm
calculate-area.s1b: Measure the sizes the shape needs with one unit, for example all in metres. For a room, measure wall to wall at floor level.
calculate-area.s2t: Pick the formula for the shape
calculate-area.s2b: Rectangle: length × width. Triangle: ½ × base × height, where the height is at right angles to the base. Circle: π × r². Trapezoid: (a + b) / 2 × h. The calculator shows the formula for each of its 12 shapes.
calculate-area.s3b: Choose the shape and the unit, then enter each size. A 5 m by 3 m room gives 15 m². If you only know a triangle's three sides, use Triangle (three sides): Heron's formula needs no height.
calculate-area.s4b: The result is listed in other units too. 1 m² is 10.764 ft², 1 ft² is 0.0929 m², an acre is 43,560 ft² and a hectare is 10,000 m². Converting lengths first and then squaring gives the same answer.
calculate-area.s5b: An L-shaped room is two rectangles: work out each and add them. Take away the area of a hole, a pillar or a pond. A curved bed edge is close to part of a circle (a sector).
calculate-area.s6b: For materials, add waste: about 10% for tiles and flooring, more for diagonal patterns. Check the answer is sensible: a 5 m × 3 m room cannot be 150 m².
calculate-area.diagram1: Formulas for the three shapes you will use most.
calculate-area.diagram2: One square metre is about 10.76 square feet.

calculate-volume.name: How to calculate volume
calculate-volume.blurb: Volume formulas for boxes, cylinders, spheres and cones.
calculate-volume.title: How to calculate volume
calculate-volume.lead: Volume tells you how much a tank, a box, a pot or a room holds, how much concrete or soil to order, or what a parcel measures. You will measure, pick the formula, keep one unit and turn the answer into litres or gallons.
calculate-volume.result: The volume in cubic units, the surface area, and the same volume in litres, millilitres, US or imperial gallons and cups.
calculate-volume.note: Volume is in a unit cubed: centimetres give cm³. 1,000 cm³ is exactly 1 litre.
calculate-volume.s1t: Open the Volume calculator on cv.cm
calculate-volume.s1b: Measure with one unit. For how much a container holds, measure the inside; for how much material you need, the outside.
calculate-volume.s2t: Pick the formula for the solid
calculate-volume.s2b: Box: length × width × height. Cylinder: π × r² × h. Sphere: 4/3 × π × r³. Cone and pyramid: one third of the matching cylinder or box. The calculator covers 12 solids.
calculate-volume.s3b: Choose the solid and unit, then enter each size. A box 30 × 20 × 10 cm gives 6,000 cm³. Use the radius, which is half the diameter, for round shapes.
calculate-volume.s4b: Surface area is the outside skin: what you would paint, wrap or insulate. A 30 × 20 × 10 cm box has 2,200 cm² of surface.
calculate-volume.s5b: 1 cm³ = 1 mL and 1,000 cm³ = 1 L, so 6,000 cm³ is 6 L. One cubic metre is 1,000 L. A US gallon is 3.785 L and an imperial gallon 4.546 L; a cubic foot is 28.3 L.
calculate-volume.s6b: A tank is rarely filled to the brim, and walls take space: subtract the wall thickness from each inside size. For concrete or soil add 5–10% for waste and settling.
calculate-volume.diagram2: A 10 cm cube holds exactly one litre.

pick-random-letter.name: How to pick a random letter
pick-random-letter.blurb: Fair letters for word games, classes and naming.
pick-random-letter.title: How to pick a random letter
pick-random-letter.lead: Word games like Scattergories, spelling drills, team names and icebreakers all start with a fair letter. You will decide which letters can come up, leave out the awkward ones, draw one or several, avoid repeats and keep a record.
pick-random-letter.result: One letter or a list of letters, each equally likely, with the last ten draws kept on the page.
pick-random-letter.note: Each draw is independent: after an A, the next letter is still 1 in 26 to be A again, unless No repeats is on.
pick-random-letter.s1t: Open the Random letter generator on cv.cm
pick-random-letter.s1b: Decide what the letter is for. A word game needs letters that start many words; a spelling drill may need only vowels.
pick-random-letter.s2t: Choose the letters that can come up
pick-random-letter.s2b: Pick the alphabet (English A–Z by default), then All letters, Vowels only or Consonants only. The line under the options lists exactly which letters are in the draw.
pick-random-letter.s3b: Type letters into Leave out, such as Q X Z for word games, where few words start with them. Spaces and commas between them are fine; case does not matter.
pick-random-letter.s4t: Draw several with or without repeats
pick-random-letter.s4b: Set How many. Tick No repeats for a list where every letter is different, for example a random order of the whole alphabet; leave it off for independent draws.
pick-random-letter.s5b: Press Draw. Each letter comes from the browser's cryptographic random generator, so none is more likely than another. Choose upper, lower or mixed case and how to separate several letters.
pick-random-letter.s6b: The last ten draws are listed under the result, so you can see what has come up in a game. Copy puts the latest letters on the clipboard.
pick-random-letter.diagram1: Only the letters left in the pool can be drawn.
pick-random-letter.diagram2: With No repeats, each drawn letter leaves the pool.

unscramble-words.name: How to unscramble letters into words
unscramble-words.blurb: Every word from your rack, blanks included.
unscramble-words.title: How to unscramble letters into words
unscramble-words.lead: A rack of seven tiles, a crossword clue with a few known letters or an anagram puzzle all come down to the same question: which words can these letters spell? You will type the letters, add blanks, narrow the list and pick the best word.
