oil.q1: How many liters are in an oil barrel?
oil.a1: One petroleum barrel is 42 US gallons, which is 158.987294928 liters.
oil.a2: No. The conversion stays in this tab.
oil.q3: Is a US gallon the same as a litre bottle?
oil.a3: A US gallon is 3.785411784 liters. It is not an imperial gallon.
oil.q4: Why is there no oil price?
oil.a4: This page only converts volume. It does not fetch a price.
oil.a5: Yes. Copy puts barrels, gallons, and liters on the clipboard.

stocks.q1: Which share count does market cap use?
stocks.a1: Company market cap is price times shares outstanding. Do not type the shares in your account.
stocks.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
stocks.q3: What if earnings per share are zero?
stocks.a3: P/E stays blank. The page does not show infinity.
stocks.q4: What if the price is zero?
stocks.a4: Dividend yield stays blank because the divisor is zero.
stocks.q5: Does this page show a stock price?
stocks.a5: No. You type the price. It is arithmetic, not a recommendation.

gamesFlash.q1: Can I play Flash games in the browser?
gamesFlash.a1: Yes. This page runs SWF files with Ruffle, an open-source Flash emulator. You do not install Adobe Flash Player.
gamesFlash.q2: What if there is no game file?
gamesFlash.a2: The player says to upload one. Choose a SWF. The file stays in this tab and is not sent to a server.
gamesFlash.q3: Why does a SWF fail to start?
gamesFlash.a3: Many games are more than one file, or they only run on the original website. This page is for a single SWF that can run alone. Some ActionScript 3 games are still incomplete.
gamesFlash.q4: Does Flash work on a phone?
gamesFlash.a4: It opens. Touch is treated as the mouse. Games that need hover or a keyboard are easier on a computer.
gamesFlash.q5: Can I download classic Flash games here?
gamesFlash.a5: No. Use a SWF you already have. cv.cm will only host a SWF when its license allows redistribution.

mosaic.a1: No. The photo stays in this tab. The canvas replaces the pixels here. Closing the tab discards it. Export also strips EXIF.
mosaic.a2: Use a black box for ID numbers, card numbers, and QR codes. A fine mosaic can sometimes be guessed back. Use mosaic for faces and background clutter.
mosaic.q3: Can I redact a chat screenshot?
mosaic.a3: Yes. Drop the screenshot and drag over avatars, names, and phone numbers. Draw as many boxes as you need; Undo removes the last one. With several photos, each keeps its own boxes and you can download a ZIP.
mosaic.q4: Can I add a watermark after redacting?
mosaic.a4: Yes. On the same page, add a “for [org] use only” mark. Redaction is applied first, then the mark.
mosaic.a5: No. This only covers areas. It cannot restore pixels someone else covered. In your export the covered pixels are replaced, not hidden.

dice.a1: Yes. Pick how many dice and which die, then press Roll. Each face and the total appear on the right.
dice.a2: No. The rolls happen in this tab.
dice.a3: d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20, and d100, up to 50 dice at once. 2d6 means two six-sided dice.
dice.a4: Each roll uses the browser's cryptographic random generator, so every face has the same chance. Nothing is seeded or stored.
dice.a5: Yes. Set a number of coins and press Flip. The tab shows each face and the heads and tails counts.

gpa.q1: Can I calculate my GPA here?
gpa.a1: Yes. Pick a letter grade and credits for each course. The GPA updates as you type.
gpa.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
gpa.a3: Each grade becomes points: A 4.0, A- 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, down to F 0. Points times credits are added up and divided by the total credits.
gpa.a4: By default A+ is 4.0. Tick A+ = 4.3 if your school uses that scale.
gpa.a5: A course with 0 or blank credits is skipped. Pass/fail courses usually do not count toward GPA.

pomodoro.q1: Can I run a Pomodoro timer here?
pomodoro.a1: Yes. Press Start. The tab counts down a focus session, chimes, and moves to a break by itself.
pomodoro.a2: No. The timer runs in this tab. Nothing is sent or stored.
pomodoro.a3: Work in focused blocks, usually 25 minutes, then rest 5 minutes. After four blocks take a longer 15-minute break. Each block is one pomodoro.
pomodoro.a4: Yes. Set focus, short break, and long break in minutes from 1 to 180, and the number of rounds before a long break. While the clock is stopped the current phase takes the new length right away; Reset starts over from round 1.
pomodoro.q5: What happens if I switch tabs?
pomodoro.a5: The timer keeps counting from the clock, and the tab title shows the time left. Keep the tab open to hear the chime.

sleep.q1: How does the sleep calculator work?
sleep.a1: Sleep runs in cycles of about 90 minutes. The tool counts back from your wake-up time (or forward from your bedtime) in whole cycles and adds about 14 minutes to fall asleep, so an alarm lands at the end of a cycle instead of in deep sleep.
sleep.a2: No. The times are computed in this tab and nothing is sent or stored.
sleep.q3: How many cycles should I sleep?
sleep.a3: Five or six cycles (7.5 to 9 hours) suit most adults. Three or four cycles are shown for short nights; use them when you must, not every night.
sleep.a4: Most people take 10 to 20 minutes to fall asleep. The calculator uses 14 minutes as an average; if you drop off faster or slower, shift the result by the difference.
sleep.a5: No. Cycles range from about 70 to 120 minutes and change through the night, so treat the times as a starting point and adjust by how you feel on waking.

body-fat.q1: How is body fat estimated here?
body-fat.a1: With the U.S. Navy circumference method: height, neck and waist for men, plus hips for women, go into a logarithmic formula. Add weight to split the result into fat mass and lean mass.
body-fat.a2: No. The measurements stay in this tab and are not stored.
body-fat.a3: Neck just below the larynx, tape sloping slightly down to the front. Waist at the navel for men and at the narrowest point for women. Hips at the widest point. Keep the tape snug but not tight.
body-fat.a4: Usually within 3 to 4 percentage points of a DEXA scan for most adults, less for very muscular or very lean people. Measure in the morning and repeat the same way to track change over time.
body-fat.a5: The ACE ranges: for men essential 2–5%, athletes 6–13%, fitness 14–17%, average 18–24%, obese 25%+; for women essential 10–13%, athletes 14–20%, fitness 21–24%, average 25–31%, obese 32%+.

contrast.q1: What does the contrast ratio mean?
contrast.a1: It compares the relative luminance of the text color and the background on a scale from 1:1 (same color) to 21:1 (black on white), as defined by WCAG 2.
contrast.a2: No. The ratio is computed in this tab.
contrast.a3: WCAG AA asks for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; AAA asks for 7:1 and 4.5:1. Icons, borders and form controls need 3:1 (non-text contrast).
contrast.a5: When the pair fails AA for normal text, the text color is moved step by step toward black or white, whichever helps, until it reaches 4.5:1. Hue is kept as close as possible.

pace.q1: How do I use the pace calculator?
pace.a1: Pick what to solve for, choose km or miles, and fill in the other two values. Time accepts h:mm:ss or mm:ss; pace accepts m:ss.
pace.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
pace.a3: Finish times for 5K, 10K, half marathon (21.0975 km) and marathon (42.195 km) if you held the same pace the whole way. Real race times slow down over longer distances.
pace.q4: How do I convert pace per km to pace per mile?
pace.a4: Multiply by 1.609. The result shows both: 5:00 /km is about 8:03 /mi.
pace.a5: Yes. Speed in km/h or mph is shown next to the pace, so 12 km/h equals a 5:00 /km pace.

grade.q1: How is the needed score calculated?
grade.a1: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight, with the weight of the final as a fraction. With 85% now, a 90% goal and a 30% final you need 101.7%.
grade.a2: No. The numbers stay in this tab.
grade.q3: What if the result is over 100%?
grade.a3: The goal is out of reach on the final alone unless there is extra credit. Check the table for the highest letter that is still possible.
grade.q4: What if the result is 0% or less?
grade.a4: You already have the grade you want. Any score on the final keeps it.
grade.a5: Your average on everything graded so far, as a percentage, before the final. If your syllabus lists category weights, use the weighted average your gradebook shows.

due-date.q1: How is the due date calculated?
due-date.a1: With Naegele's rule: 280 days (40 weeks) after the first day of the last period for a 28-day cycle. A longer or shorter cycle shifts the date by the difference, so a 32-day cycle adds 4 days.
due-date.a2: No. The dates are computed in this tab and nothing is stored.
due-date.q3: What if I know the conception date instead?
due-date.a3: Pick Conception date. The due date is 266 days after it. If you already have a due date from a scan, pick Due date to see the weeks and trimesters.
due-date.a4: Only about 4% of babies arrive on the due date; most come within two weeks either side. An early ultrasound gives the most reliable date and overrides this estimate.
due-date.a5: The second trimester starts at 13 weeks + 0 days and the third at 27 weeks + 0 days, counted from the last period. Different books use slightly different cut-offs.

ideal-weight.a1: Devine (1974), Robinson (1983), Miller (1983) and Hamwi (1964). Each gives a base weight at 5 feet and adds a fixed amount per inch above it, with separate numbers for men and women.
ideal-weight.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
ideal-weight.a3: They were fitted to different groups, mostly for drug dosing and insurance tables, so they differ by a few kilograms. Treat the spread as the range, not any single number as the target.
ideal-weight.q4: What is the BMI range row?
ideal-weight.a4: The weights that give a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 at your height, the WHO healthy range for adults. It does not account for muscle mass or age.
ideal-weight.a5: The formulas are defined from 5 feet (152.4 cm) upward; below that the tool extrapolates the same per-inch step down to 140 cm, so treat those results as rough.

water-intake.a1: About 35 ml per kilogram of body weight, plus about 12 ml per minute of exercise, plus 500 ml in hot or humid weather. A 70 kg person with 30 minutes of exercise gets about 2.8 litres.
water-intake.a2: No. The numbers stay in this tab.
water-intake.q3: Does the total include food and other drinks?
water-intake.a3: It is total fluid. Roughly a fifth usually comes from food, and tea, coffee and milk count toward it.
water-intake.a4: No. It is a rule of thumb for healthy adults. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or heart conditions and some medicines change the need; ask a doctor.
water-intake.a5: 250 ml, about 8.5 US fluid ounces. The glass count is rounded up.

fuel-cost.q1: How is the fuel cost calculated?
fuel-cost.a1: Distance is turned into litres with your car's economy, then multiplied by the price per litre. 300 km at 7 L/100 km uses 21 litres; at 1.60 a litre that is 33.60.
fuel-cost.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
fuel-cost.a3: L/100 km, km/L and US mpg. Price can be per litre or per US gallon; the tool converts between them.
fuel-cost.q4: How do I split the cost?
fuel-cost.a4: Enter the number of people. Cost per person divides the total evenly, including the driver.
fuel-cost.q5: Why is the real cost higher?
fuel-cost.a5: Economy figures are for mixed driving; city traffic, air conditioning, roof racks and a loaded car use more. Add about 10% for a safe estimate.

reading-time.a1: Words divided by a reading speed: 150 words a minute for slow, 238 for average adult silent reading, 300 for fast. Speaking time uses 130 words a minute.
reading-time.a2: No. The text stays in this tab.
reading-time.q3: How are Chinese, Japanese and Korean counted?
reading-time.a3: In characters, not words: 200, 300 or 400 characters a minute for reading and 180 for speaking. Mixed text counts Latin words and CJK characters separately.
reading-time.q4: Is the average speed right for me?
reading-time.a4: 238 words a minute is the mean for adults reading non-fiction in English (Brysbaert, 2019). Technical text is slower; pick Slow for it.
reading-time.q5: Can I use it for a speech?
reading-time.a5: Yes. The speaking row uses a conversational 130 words a minute. Presenters often speak 110–150, so adjust by a minute or two for pauses.

time-card.a1: For each shift, end time minus start time minus the unpaid break. 09:00 to 17:30 with a 30-minute break is 8 hours. The week's shifts are added up.
time-card.a2: No. The times stay in this tab and are not stored.
time-card.a3: Yes. If the end time is earlier than the start, the shift runs past midnight: 22:00 to 06:00 is 8 hours. A moon mark shows next to those rows.
time-card.a4: Hours above the weekly threshold, 40 by default, are overtime and paid at the multiplier, 1.5 by default. Overtime rules differ by country and contract; set the threshold and multiplier to match yours.
time-card.q5: How do I convert hours and minutes to decimal hours?
time-card.a5: Divide the minutes by 60: 7:30 is 7.5 hours, 7:45 is 7.75. The totals show both forms.

electricity.a1: Watts × hours a day ÷ 1000 gives kWh a day; kWh × your price per kWh gives the cost. A 1000 W air conditioner for 8 hours uses 8 kWh; at 0.15 a kWh that is 1.20 a day.
electricity.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
electricity.q3: Where do I find the watts?
electricity.a3: On the label or plug of the appliance, or in its manual. Devices that cycle on and off, like fridges and air conditioners, draw full power only part of the time, so their real use is usually lower than the label.
electricity.q4: Where do I find my price per kWh?
electricity.a4: On your electricity bill: total energy charge divided by kWh used. Tiered or time-of-use tariffs have several prices; use the one for the hours the appliance runs.
electricity.a5: Enter the standby watts (often 0.5–5 W) with 24 hours a day. 5 W all year is about 44 kWh.

ovulation.q1: How is the ovulation day estimated?
ovulation.a1: Ovulation usually happens about 14 days before the next period. With a 28-day cycle that is day 14; with a 32-day cycle, day 18.
ovulation.a2: No. The dates stay in this tab and are not stored.
ovulation.a3: The five days before ovulation plus ovulation day. Sperm can survive up to five days and the egg about a day, so these six days carry the highest chance of pregnancy.
ovulation.q4: Can I use this as contraception?
ovulation.a4: No. Cycles vary, and calendar estimates miss many ovulations. Use a reliable method of contraception, and ask a doctor if you are planning a pregnancy.
ovulation.q5: My cycle is irregular. Will it work?
ovulation.a5: Less well. Use the average length of your last six cycles. Ovulation tests or basal temperature tracking give a better signal for irregular cycles.

macro.a1: The calorie target is split by percentages and divided by calories per gram: protein 4, fat 9, carbohydrate 4. 2500 kcal at 30/30/40 is 188 g protein, 83 g fat and 250 g carbs.
macro.a2: No. The numbers stay in this tab.
macro.q3: Where does the calorie target come from?
macro.a3: Use your maintenance calories (TDEE). The TDEE calculator on cv.cm estimates it; the goal then subtracts 500 kcal to lose weight or adds 300 to gain.
macro.a4: Balanced (30/30/40) suits most people. High protein (40/30/30) helps keep muscle while losing weight. Low carb (35/45/20) suits people who prefer fewer carbohydrates.
macro.q5: How much protein do I need?
macro.a5: Active adults often aim for 1.6–2.2 g per kg of body weight. Enter your weight to see the protein per kg for the chosen split.

calories-burned.a1: Calories = MET × body weight in kg × hours. A MET is the energy of an activity relative to rest. Brisk walking is 4.3 MET, so 30 minutes at 70 kg burns about 151 kcal.
calories-burned.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
calories-burned.q3: Where do the MET values come from?
calories-burned.a3: From the 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities (Ainsworth et al.), the standard reference used in research and fitness apps.
calories-burned.a4: Within about 20% for most people. Fitness, effort, terrain and body composition all change the real number. Treat it as an estimate.
calories-burned.q5: Does it include calories I would burn anyway?
calories-burned.a5: Yes. MET includes resting energy. Subtract about 1 kcal per kg per hour to see only the extra calories from the activity.

remove-background.a1: Yes. There is no sign-up, watermark or limit. The AI model downloads once and then runs on your own device.
remove-background.a2: No. The model runs in this browser tab with WebGPU or WebAssembly. Photos never leave your device, and closing the tab discards them.
remove-background.a3: Clear subjects: people, products, pets, cars, furniture. Fine hair and glass are harder; a plain, contrasting background helps.
remove-background.q4: Can I remove backgrounds from many images at once?
remove-background.a4: Yes. Drop several photos; they are processed one after another, and Download all saves a ZIP.
remove-background.q5: Can I put a new background behind the subject?
remove-background.a5: Choose transparent, white, any color, or a blurred copy of the original. Transparent needs PNG or WebP; JPG adds white.

image-upscaler.q1: How does the AI upscaler work?
image-upscaler.a1: It runs Real-ESRGAN, a super-resolution network, on your GPU or CPU. It enlarges 4× and redraws edges and textures; 2× averages that down for a cleaner result.
image-upscaler.a2: No. The 2–5 MB model downloads once; the image is processed in this tab and never leaves your device.
image-upscaler.a3: Up to about 16 megapixels (for example 4096 × 4096), the limit Safari can draw. Bigger inputs are scaled to fit first.
image-upscaler.a4: Photo suits camera pictures and screenshots. Anime / art keeps flat colors and outlines in illustrations, comics and game art.
image-upscaler.q5: Can it recover details that were never there?
image-upscaler.a5: No upscaler can. It makes pictures sharper and cleaner, but small text or faces it cannot see are guessed, not restored.

speech-to-text.q1: Is this speech to text free?
speech-to-text.a1: Yes, with no sign-up or minutes limit. It uses OpenAI's open Whisper model, which downloads once and runs on your device.
speech-to-text.a2: No. Audio and video are decoded and transcribed in this tab. Nothing is sent to a server, which suits private meetings and interviews.
speech-to-text.a3: Whisper knows 99 languages, including English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Indonesian and Spanish. It can detect the language or translate the speech into English.
speech-to-text.a4: Yes. Download SRT or VTT with timestamps for YouTube, Premiere, CapCut or a video player, or plain TXT.
speech-to-text.q5: How long can a file be?
speech-to-text.a5: Hours are fine; the audio is read in 30-second windows. Speed depends on your device: with a GPU, an hour usually takes a few minutes.

depth-map.a1: A grayscale image where brightness shows distance: near is white, far is black. 3D tools use it for parallax, depth of field and relighting.
depth-map.a2: Depth Anything V2 Small (Apache-2.0). It downloads once (about 25–100 MB, depending on your device) and runs in this tab.
depth-map.a3: No. The photo is processed in your browser and never leaves your device.
depth-map.q4: Can I use it with ControlNet or Blender?
depth-map.a4: Yes. Download the grayscale PNG for a ControlNet depth input, a Blender displacement map or a 3D photo effect.
depth-map.a5: No. It is relative depth: it orders what is nearer or farther, not measured distance.

wheel.a1: Yes. The winner is drawn with Web Crypto before the wheel moves, and every entry has the same chance. The spin only shows the result.
wheel.a2: Type one name or option per line in the list. Up to 100 entries; repeat a line to give it a bigger slice.
wheel.a3: Tick “Remove the winner after each spin” to draw names one by one without repeats, for example to set a speaking order.
wheel.a4: No. The list and the draw stay in this tab.
wheel.q5: Can I use it for a giveaway?
wheel.a5: Yes, for casual draws. Share your screen while you spin. For draws with legal rules, follow the rules where you live.

average.q1: What is the difference between mean, median and mode?
average.a1: The mean is the sum divided by the count. The median is the middle value after sorting (the mean of the two middle values for an even count). The mode is the value that appears most often.
average.a2: Use the sample value (divides by n − 1) when your numbers are a sample of a bigger group, and the population value (divides by n) when they are the whole group.
average.a3: Separate them with spaces, new lines or semicolons. With the decimal mark set to a dot (3.5), commas separate numbers too; set it to a comma for 3,5. You can paste a column from a spreadsheet.
average.a4: When every value appears the same number of times, for example all different, no value is the mode.
average.a5: No. The numbers stay in this tab.

metronome.q1: How do I use the metronome?
metronome.a1: Set the BPM, choose the beats per bar and press Start. The first beat of each bar is higher when the accent is on.
metronome.a2: Press Tap in time with a song four or more times; the BPM follows the average of your last taps. A pause of two seconds starts over.
metronome.a3: Clicks are scheduled on the Web Audio clock, not with timers, so they stay steady even when the page is busy.
metronome.a4: Check the volume slider, the device volume and the silent switch on phones. Some browsers pause audio in background tabs.
metronome.q5: What do Andante and Allegro mean?
metronome.a5: They are Italian tempo marks. Andante is a walking pace (about 76–108 BPM), Allegro is fast (about 120–156 BPM).

keyboard-test.q1: How do I test my keyboard?
keyboard-test.a1: Click the keyboard picture, then press every key. Keys that work turn pink; the one you are holding turns dark.
keyboard-test.q2: A key does not light up. Is it broken?
keyboard-test.a2: Not always. Fn, some media keys and keys the system reserves (like Print Screen on some computers) never reach the browser. Try the key in a text field too.
keyboard-test.a3: How many keys the keyboard reports at once. Hold several keys together; “Most at once” shows the highest number seen.
keyboard-test.q4: What do key, code and keyCode mean?
keyboard-test.a4: key is the character or name the key produces, code is the physical key position, and keyCode is the older numeric code many games still use.
keyboard-test.a5: No. Key presses are shown in this tab only and are not sent anywhere.

zodiac.a1: Enter your birthday. The tool shows your star sign (Western zodiac), its date range and element.
zodiac.q2: What is my Chinese zodiac animal?
zodiac.a2: It follows the lunar year, which starts on Lunar New Year between 21 January and 20 February. If you were born before that day, your animal is the previous year’s.
zodiac.q3: Why do sign dates differ between sites?
zodiac.a3: The Sun enters each sign at a slightly different time each year, so the first day can move by one. If you were born on the edge, check an ephemeris for your birth year.
zodiac.a4: In the Chinese calendar each year has an element (wood, fire, earth, metal or water) and is yin or yang; together with the animal they give the 60-year cycle, such as 甲辰 (wood dragon) for 2024.
zodiac.a5: No. The date stays in this tab.

click-test.a1: CPS means clicks per second. Click the pad as fast as you can until the time runs out; your clicks are divided by the seconds of the test.
click-test.a2: Most people click 5–8 times a second with one finger. 8–11 is fast, and above 11 usually takes jitter or butterfly clicking.
click-test.q3: Which test length should I pick?
click-test.a3: 5 seconds is the usual test. 1 second measures a short burst; 30 and 60 seconds show how well you keep the pace.
click-test.a4: Yes: with the pad focused, each press of Space or Enter counts once. Holding the key down does not repeat.
click-test.a5: Your best score for each length is shown until you close the tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.

reaction-time.q1: How does the reaction time test work?
reaction-time.a1: Click the pad to start. It turns red; after a random 1.5–4.5 seconds it turns green. Click as soon as you see green. The time between green and your click is your reaction time.
reaction-time.q2: What is a normal reaction time?
reaction-time.a2: Most people react to a visual signal in about 200–300 ms with a mouse or touch screen. Under 200 ms is fast.
reaction-time.a3: Single tries vary a lot. The average and median of five give a steadier number; the best and worst are shown too.
reaction-time.q4: Does my device change the result?
reaction-time.a4: Yes. Screen refresh, mouse or touch latency and browser load add a few to tens of milliseconds, so compare results on the same device.
reaction-time.q5: What if I click too early?
reaction-time.a5: Clicking while the pad is red shows “Too soon” and the try does not count. Click again to retry it.

tone-generator.q1: What can I use a tone generator for?
tone-generator.a1: To test speakers and headphones, check left and right channels, find a rattle or hum, tune an instrument to A4 = 440 Hz, or try the range of your hearing.
tone-generator.a2: Sine is a pure tone, best for tests. Square, triangle and sawtooth add harmonics and sound buzzier.
tone-generator.q3: Why can't I hear very low or very high tones?
tone-generator.a3: Small speakers rarely play below about 80 Hz, and hearing above 15–17 kHz fades with age. Your device's audio path may cut them too.
tone-generator.q4: Is it safe for my ears and speakers?
tone-generator.a4: Start at a low volume, especially with headphones and high frequencies. Volume starts at 20% for that reason. Stop if it hurts.
tone-generator.a5: The tone is made in your browser with Web Audio; once the page has loaded, nothing else is downloaded or uploaded.

tally-counter.a1: Press + or − on a counter, or use the keyboard: Space, ↑ or + adds, ↓ or − subtracts on the highlighted counter.
tally-counter.a2: Yes. Add up to 12 counters, give each a name and see the total of all of them.
tally-counter.q3: Can I count by more than one?
tally-counter.a3: Set the step (1–1000). Each press then adds or subtracts that amount.
tally-counter.a4: Yes, in this browser only (local storage). They come back when you reopen the page; private windows may forget them.
tally-counter.q5: Can the count go below zero?
tally-counter.a5: Only if you tick “Allow negative numbers”. Otherwise counters stop at 0.

mic-test.q1: How do I test my microphone?
mic-test.a1: Press Start microphone and allow access. Speak: the meter and waveform should move. Record 5 seconds and play it back to hear how you sound.
mic-test.q2: The meter does not move. What now?
mic-test.a2: Pick another device in the list, check that the microphone is not muted (some headsets have a switch), and close other apps that use it. On a laptop, check the system's input volume.
mic-test.a3: Speech peaks around −20 to −6 dBFS are good. Near 0 dBFS the sound clips; below −20 it is quiet.
mic-test.a4: No. The audio and the test recording stay in this tab and are gone when you close it.
mic-test.q5: Why does the browser ask for permission?
mic-test.a5: Browsers only give a page the microphone after you allow it. You can take the permission back in the site settings at any time.

webcam-test.q1: How do I test my webcam?
webcam-test.a1: Press Start camera and allow access. You should see yourself in the preview; the panel shows the camera's name, the real resolution and the frame rate. Take a photo to check sharpness and colour.
webcam-test.q2: The preview is black or the camera is not found. What now?
webcam-test.a2: Close other apps that use the camera (video calls, OBS), check the privacy shutter or the camera key on your laptop, pick another camera in the list, and allow camera access for the browser in your system settings.
webcam-test.q3: Why is the resolution lower than I chose?
webcam-test.a3: Your camera does not offer that size, so the browser picks its nearest mode. The panel always shows the size you actually get.
webcam-test.q4: Why is the frame rate low?
webcam-test.a4: Most webcams drop to 15 fps or less in dim light to expose longer. Add light, or pick a lower resolution; USB 2.0 hubs can limit 1080p too.
webcam-test.a5: No. The video stays in this tab, and photos are made on your device. Nothing is sent or stored.

gamepad-test.q1: How do I test my controller?
gamepad-test.a1: Connect it by USB or Bluetooth and press any button: browsers only show a controller after a button press. Then press every button and move both sticks; each button lights up while pressed and stays marked once it has worked.
gamepad-test.q2: How do I check stick drift?
gamepad-test.a2: Let go of both sticks. A healthy stick reads close to 0.00; above 0.05 is slight drift that most games hide with a dead zone, and 0.15 or more usually shows in games.
gamepad-test.a3: Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro and most USB or Bluetooth gamepads. With a “standard” layout the buttons get their names; other pads show numbered buttons and axes.
gamepad-test.q4: Why does Test vibration not work?
gamepad-test.a4: Vibration needs a browser that supports it (Chrome and Edge do) and a controller with motors. Some Bluetooth connections do not pass it through.
gamepad-test.a5: No. The controller is read in this tab with the Gamepad API; nothing is sent or stored.

dead-pixel.q1: How do I check for dead pixels?
dead-pixel.a1: Clean the screen, press Start full screen test and look closely at each colour. A dead pixel stays black on white, a stuck pixel stays one colour (often red, green or blue), and a hot pixel stays white on black.
dead-pixel.a2: Dust and smudges move or blur when you wipe the screen or change your viewing angle; a bad pixel stays sharp in the same spot on every colour it should change on.
dead-pixel.q3: Can a stuck pixel be fixed?
dead-pixel.a3: Sometimes: a stuck pixel can come back after hours of normal use. Dead pixels usually stay. This page does not flash colours quickly, which can trigger seizures.
dead-pixel.q4: How do I move between colours?
dead-pixel.a4: Click or tap, or press Space or →, for the next colour; ← goes back. Tap the left third of a touch screen to go back. Esc or × closes the test.
dead-pixel.a5: Yes. Where full screen is not available (iPhone), the colour covers the whole browser window; hide the toolbars by scrolling or turning the phone.

refresh-rate.q1: How does the refresh rate test work?
refresh-rate.a1: The page counts how often the browser draws a frame. Browsers draw once per screen refresh, so the time between frames gives the refresh rate in Hz.
refresh-rate.q2: Why does it show 60 Hz on my 144 Hz monitor?
refresh-rate.a2: Check the rate set in your system's display settings, the cable (older HDMI caps at 60 Hz at high resolutions) and battery saver. With two screens, the browser follows the one its window is on.
refresh-rate.a3: Frames that took about twice as long as normal: the screen showed the previous frame again. A few are normal while the page loads; many mean the computer or browser is busy.
refresh-rate.q4: What is the moving block for?
refresh-rate.a4: At a higher refresh rate the block moves in smaller steps and looks smoother and sharper. Compare speeds to see judder or blur.
refresh-rate.q5: Why did the number change when I switched tabs?
refresh-rate.a5: Hidden tabs get few or no frames, so the test starts over when you come back. Keep the tab in front for a few seconds for a steady reading.

touch-test.q1: How do I test my touch screen?
touch-test.a1: Put fingers on the pad and draw. Each finger gets its own colour and number. Then swipe over the whole pad: cells you have touched fill in, and any that will not fill show a dead zone.
touch-test.q2: How many fingers does my screen support?
touch-test.a2: Put down as many fingers as you can at once and read Most at once. Phones and tablets usually track 5–10; some laptops track only 2.
touch-test.a3: Most touch screens and mice do not measure pressure. Pens such as Apple Pencil and Surface Pen usually do.
touch-test.q4: Can I test the edges of the screen?
touch-test.a4: Press Full screen so the pad fills the screen, then swipe along every edge and corner.
touch-test.a5: No. Touches are drawn in this tab and forgotten when you clear or close it.

v.q1: How does photo to video work?
v.a1: An AI model (Depth Anything V2) estimates how far each part of the picture is. A virtual camera then moves through that depth, so near things shift more than the background, like a short 3D shot.
v.a2: No. The model downloads once (about 25–100 MB, depending on your device) and runs in this tab. The video is encoded in the browser too.
v.q3: Can it make a video from text?
v.a3: No. It animates a picture you already have: a photo, a drawing or an AI image. People and objects do not move on their own; the camera moves.
v.q4: Which format and size is the video?
v.a4: MP4 at 30 fps, 3, 5 or 8 seconds, 720p or 1080p (never more than the photo's own pixels), in the photo's shape or cropped to 9:16, 1:1 or 16:9. It plays on phones and uploads to TikTok, Reels and Shorts.
v.a5: The camera reveals a little of what was hidden behind near objects, and the tool fills it from nearby pixels. Pick Subtle, or a photo with a clear subject and a plain background.

ai-image-generator.q1: How does the AI image generator work?
ai-image-generator.a1: Janus-Pro-1B, an open model from DeepSeek, reads your text and draws a 384 × 384 picture token by token. Real-ESRGAN can then enlarge it to 768 or 1536 px. Both run in this tab. Prompts in other languages are first translated to English by OPUS-MT (Helsinki-NLP, CC BY 4.0 / Apache-2.0), about 110 MB per language, also in this tab.
ai-image-generator.q2: Is it free? Is there a watermark?
ai-image-generator.a2: Free, no account, no daily limit and no watermark: the work runs on your own device, so there is no server cost to charge for.
ai-image-generator.q3: Can I use the images commercially?
ai-image-generator.a3: Yes. The DeepSeek Model License allows commercial use. It forbids some uses, such as illegal content, content that harms minors, disinformation and harassment, so those are not allowed here either.
ai-image-generator.q4: Why is the first image slow?
ai-image-generator.a4: The model downloads once (about 1.5 GB) and is kept in your browser. After that, an image takes from a few seconds to about a minute, depending on your graphics card.
ai-image-generator.q5: Why does it say WebGPU is needed?
ai-image-generator.a5: Drawing needs a graphics card through WebGPU (recent Chrome, Edge or Safari). On the CPU alone one image would take many minutes, so the page does not start it.

ai-music-generator.q1: How does the AI music generator work?
ai-music-generator.a1: MusicVAE, an open model from Google's Magenta project, writes 4 bars of melody, bass and drums at a time; longer pieces morph from one idea to another. The page then plays the notes with its own synthesizers.
ai-music-generator.q2: Can I use the music in videos or commercially?
ai-music-generator.a2: Yes. Every piece is newly generated, the model is Apache-2.0, and nothing is sampled from existing songs. Use it in videos, games, podcasts or products, no credit needed.
ai-music-generator.q3: Does it make songs with vocals?
ai-music-generator.a3: No. It makes instrumental music: a lead melody, a bass line and drums. Download the MIDI file to play the same notes with other instruments in GarageBand, FL Studio or any DAW.
ai-music-generator.a4: No. The model downloads once (about 18 MB) and runs in this tab; the audio is rendered in the browser too.
ai-music-generator.q5: How do I get music I like?
ai-music-generator.a5: Generate a few times and keep the one you like, then press More like this for variations of it. Calm keeps the music simple and repetitive; Wild tries bolder ideas.

coin-flip.a1: Yes. Each flip takes one random bit from your browser's cryptographic random number generator (Web Crypto), so heads and tails each have exactly a 50% chance and earlier flips never affect the next one.
coin-flip.q2: Can I flip several coins at once?
coin-flip.a2: Yes. Pick 10, 100 or 1,000 coins under Coins per flip. The result says how many came up heads and tails, and every coin is added to the counts.
coin-flip.q3: Why do I sometimes get many heads in a row?
coin-flip.a3: Streaks are normal. In 100 fair flips the longest run of one side is usually 5 to 7. The Longest streak line shows yours.
coin-flip.a4: Yes. Press Space or Enter to flip when the page is scrolled to the coin and no field or link is focused.
coin-flip.a5: Counts and history stay until you press Reset or leave this page. Nothing is uploaded or stored.

guitar-tuner.q1: How do I tune my guitar with this tuner?
guitar-tuner.a1: Press Start tuner and allow the microphone. Pluck one string and let it ring. The tuner shows the nearest string and a needle: left means flat (tighten the string), right means sharp (loosen it). Stop when the needle is in the green zone.
guitar-tuner.q2: What are the notes of standard guitar tuning?
guitar-tuner.a2: From the thickest string to the thinnest: E2, A2, D3, G3, B3 and E4 (82.41, 110, 146.83, 196, 246.94 and 329.63 Hz at A4 = 440 Hz).
guitar-tuner.q3: Can I tune a bass, ukulele or violin?
guitar-tuner.a3: Yes. Pick it under Instrument: 4- and 5-string bass, ukulele (G C E A), violin, cello, alternate guitar tunings such as drop D, half step down, DADGAD and open G, or Chromatic for any note.
guitar-tuner.a4: It is the pitch every other note is worked out from. Almost all music uses 440 Hz. Change it to tune to a piano or recording that sits a little higher or lower, such as 442 Hz or 432 Hz.
guitar-tuner.a5: No. The microphone is analysed in this tab only and nothing is recorded or sent. Close the tab or press Stop to turn the microphone off.

factors.q1: How do I find all the factors of a number?
factors.a1: Type the number. The page lists every divisor from smallest to largest, the factor pairs that multiply to the number and how many divisors there are.
factors.a2: Writing a number as a product of prime numbers, for example 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. Every whole number above 1 has exactly one prime factorization.
factors.q3: How do I know if a number is prime?
factors.a3: A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. The page says whether your number is prime and shows the primes just below and above it. 1 is neither prime nor composite.
factors.q4: How large a number can it factor?
factors.a4: Any whole number up to 18 digits, exactly. It uses a deterministic Miller–Rabin prime test and Pollard's rho method, so even large numbers take a fraction of a second.
factors.q5: How is the number of divisors worked out?
factors.a5: Add 1 to each exponent in the prime factorization and multiply: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5¹ has (3 + 1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 24 divisors.

lcm-gcf.q1: How do I find the LCM and GCF?
lcm-gcf.a1: Type two or more whole numbers separated by commas or spaces. The least common multiple (LCM) and greatest common factor (GCF) appear at once, with the working.
lcm-gcf.q2: Is GCF the same as GCD or HCF?
lcm-gcf.a2: Yes. Greatest common factor (GCF), greatest common divisor (GCD) and highest common factor (HCF) are three names for the largest number that divides all of them.
lcm-gcf.q3: How do prime factors give the LCM and GCF?
lcm-gcf.a3: Factor each number into primes. The GCF takes each prime that is in every number, at its lowest power; the LCM takes every prime at its highest power. For 12, 18 and 30: GCF = 2 × 3 = 6, LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 180.
lcm-gcf.a4: For two numbers, divide the larger by the smaller and keep the remainder; repeat with the smaller number and the remainder until the remainder is 0. The last divisor is the GCF. The page shows each step.
lcm-gcf.q5: When do I need the LCM?
lcm-gcf.a5: To add fractions (the LCM of the denominators is the lowest common denominator) and to find when repeating events line up, such as buses every 12 and 18 minutes meeting every 36 minutes.

calculator.q1: How do I use the scientific calculator?
calculator.a1: Type a sum or tap the keys, for example 2 × (3 + 4) or sin(30). The result shows as you type; press = or Enter to keep it in the history.
calculator.a2: The DEG/RAD button switches the angle unit for sin, cos, tan and their inverses. It starts in degrees, so sin(30) is 0.5.
calculator.q3: In what order does it calculate?
calculator.a3: Brackets first, then powers and factorials, then × and ÷, then + and −. −2^2 is −4, and 2π or 3(4 + 1) multiply without a × sign.
calculator.a4: % divides by 100: 50% is 0.5 and 200 × 15% is 30. Ans stands for the last result, so you can carry on from it.
calculator.a5: The last 20 sums are kept in this browser only, so they are there next time. Clear history removes them. Nothing is sent anywhere.

notepad.a1: In this browser's local storage, on your device. It is saved a moment after you stop typing and is there when you come back. It is never uploaded.
notepad.q2: Can I open the note on another device?
notepad.a2: No, the note stays in this browser. Download it as a .txt file, or copy it, to move it. Clearing your browsing data deletes the note.
notepad.a3: Once the page has loaded, typing and saving work without a connection, because nothing goes to a server.
notepad.q4: Can I open a text file?
notepad.a4: Yes. Open reads a .txt, .md, .csv or similar file into the notepad on your device. It replaces the note; Undo brings the old one back for a few seconds.
notepad.q5: What if I have it open in two tabs?
notepad.a5: A tab you are not typing in picks up what the other tab saved. Private windows may not keep the note after they are closed.

markdown.a1: Headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, links, images, lists, task lists, quotes, code spans and fenced code blocks, horizontal rules and GitHub-style tables.
markdown.q2: How do I convert Markdown to HTML?
markdown.a2: Paste your Markdown and press Copy HTML, or Download HTML for a complete page. The HTML is clean, with no classes or scripts added.
markdown.a3: No. Raw HTML tags are shown as text, and only web, email, phone and relative links are linked, so a pasted document cannot run scripts.
markdown.q4: Is my text saved or uploaded?
markdown.a4: Your text stays in this browser and is kept for your next visit. It is never uploaded. Images in the preview load from the addresses you write.
markdown.q5: How do I make a table?
markdown.a5: Write a header row with | between cells, then a row of dashes like |---|---|, then one line per row. Colons in the dash row set alignment: :--- left, :---: centre, ---: right.

gradient.q1: How do I make a CSS gradient?
gradient.a1: Pick a type (linear, radial or conic), set the colours and their positions, and adjust the angle or shape. The CSS updates as you go; press Copy CSS.
gradient.a2: A colour at a position along the gradient, from 0% to 100%. Add up to six stops; the gradient blends between them in order of position.
gradient.q3: Why are there two background lines?
gradient.a3: The first line is a solid colour for very old browsers; the second is the gradient. Every current browser uses the gradient.
gradient.q4: Can I save the gradient as an image?
gradient.a4: Yes. Choose a size (desktop, phone, 1440p or square) and press Save PNG. It is drawn in your browser.
gradient.a5: Linear blends along a line at an angle (90° is left to right). Radial spreads from the centre as a circle or ellipse. Conic sweeps around the centre like a colour wheel.

fancy-text.q1: How does the fancy text generator work?
fancy-text.a1: It swaps letters and numbers for look-alike Unicode characters, such as mathematical bold or circled letters. They are text, not images, so they paste anywhere.
fancy-text.q2: Where can I use these fonts?
fancy-text.a2: Instagram and TikTok bios, X posts, Discord, WhatsApp, YouTube comments and game names. Some apps or fonts may show a box for a character they lack.
fancy-text.q3: Why are some letters not changed?
fancy-text.a3: Unicode has these styles only for A–Z, a–z and some digits. Other letters, accents and Chinese, Japanese or Korean text stay as you typed them. Strikethrough and Underline are the exception: they also mark those.
fancy-text.a4: Screen readers may read them letter by letter or skip them, and search does not match them. Use them for decoration, not for important text.
fancy-text.q5: How do I copy a style?
fancy-text.a5: Type your text, then press Copy next to the style you like. Upside-down text is also reversed, so it reads correctly turned over.

rom-emulator.q1: Which consoles and files does it open?
rom-emulator.a1: FC / NES (.nes), SFC / SNES (.sfc, .smc), Game Boy and Game Boy Color (.gb, .gbc), Game Boy Advance (.gba) and Mega Drive / Genesis (.md, .gen, .smd, .bin), or a .zip holding one of these.
rom-emulator.a2: No. The file is read in this tab and handed to the emulator on this page. Only the emulator itself is downloaded.
rom-emulator.q3: Why does it ask me to choose a console?
rom-emulator.a3: SNES files have no fixed header, and a .bin or a zipped .bin can be anything. If the file does not name its console, pick one under Console and the game starts.
rom-emulator.a4: No commercial ROMs. Open a file you have the right to use. The Games column has free homebrew that starts without a file.
rom-emulator.q5: How do I play and save?
rom-emulator.a5: The controls appear once a game starts. On a phone, use the on-screen pad; a Bluetooth gamepad works too. Save and load states from the emulator toolbar.

flash-player.q1: Do I need Adobe Flash Player?
flash-player.a1: No. Ruffle, an open-source Flash emulator, runs the file in the page. There is nothing to install. This page is not from Adobe.
flash-player.a2: No. The file stays in this tab and is not sent to a server.
flash-player.q3: Why does my SWF stop on a loading screen?
flash-player.a3: This page runs a file that can start on its own. It blocks network access, so a game that loads more SWFs, XML or its old website stops there.
flash-player.a4: Most older ActionScript 1 and 2 files do. ActionScript 3 support in Ruffle is still incomplete, so some newer games fail to start or misbehave.
flash-player.a5: Browsers block audio that plays by itself. Click the picture once and the sound starts.

tier-list.a1: A chart that sorts things into ranked rows instead of giving each one a number, usually S at the top and D at the bottom. It is popular for games, anime, food and anything people like to argue about.
tier-list.q2: How do I make a tier list here?
tier-list.a2: Type one item per line or add pictures, then drag each item into a row. On a phone or with a keyboard, tap or press Enter on an item, then choose Put here on a row. Download PNG saves the chart.
tier-list.a3: No. Pictures stay in this page, and the PNG is drawn in your browser. Names and rows are remembered on this device, but pictures are not, so add them again after you reload the page.
tier-list.a4: Yes. Click a row name to rename it, change its colour, move it up or down, add rows or remove them, up to 12. Items in a removed row go back to the unranked pool.
tier-list.q5: What is the 夯 to 拉 preset?
tier-list.a5: A Chinese internet meme version of a tier list. The rows run from 夯 (the very best) through 顶级 (top), 人上人 (above average) and NPC (forgettable) to 拉完了 (the worst).

mortgage.q1: How is the monthly mortgage payment calculated?
mortgage.a1: With equal payments, M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the loan (price minus down payment), r the yearly rate ÷ 12 and n the number of months. A 320,000 loan at 6.5% for 30 years is 2,022.62 a month.
mortgage.q2: What is the difference between equal payments and equal principal?
mortgage.a2: Equal payments (an annuity, common in the US and UK) keep the same payment every month. Equal principal repays the same part of the loan each month plus that month's interest, so it starts higher, falls every month and costs less interest overall.
mortgage.q3: Does it include property tax, insurance or PMI?
mortgage.a3: No. It shows principal and interest only. Add your monthly tax, insurance and any mortgage insurance on top to get the full housing payment.
mortgage.q4: What does the amortization schedule show?
mortgage.a4: For each year, how much of what you paid went to principal and to interest, and the balance still owed at the end of that year. Early years are mostly interest with equal payments.
mortgage.a5: No. Every number is worked out in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or saved.

quadratic.q1: How do I solve a quadratic equation?
quadratic.a1: Write it as ax² + bx + c = 0 and type a, b and c. The roots come from the quadratic formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a. The page shows each step.
quadratic.q2: What does the discriminant tell me?
quadratic.a2: Δ = b² − 4ac. If it is positive there are two real roots, if it is 0 one repeated root, and if it is negative two complex roots and the parabola does not cross the x-axis.
quadratic.q3: Why are some answers shown with a square root?
quadratic.a3: When a, b and c are whole numbers the solver keeps the exact answer, such as (3 ± √5)/2 or 1/2, and gives the decimal next to it. Decimal coefficients get decimal roots.
quadratic.q4: What are the vertex and the axis of symmetry?
quadratic.a4: The vertex is the turning point of the parabola, at x = −b ÷ 2a. The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through it. If a is positive the vertex is the lowest point, if negative the highest.
quadratic.a5: Then it is not quadratic: bx + c = 0 is a linear equation with one root, x = −c ÷ b. The page gives that root instead.

team-generator.q1: How do I make random teams?
team-generator.a1: Paste names, one per line or separated by commas, choose the number of teams or people per team, and press Generate. Press it again for a new draw.
team-generator.a2: Sizes differ by at most one, and which teams get an extra person is random too. The shuffle uses your browser's cryptographic random numbers, so every split is equally likely.
team-generator.q3: What if the names do not divide evenly?
team-generator.a3: The line under the list says how it will split, for example 10 names into 3 teams gives teams of 3 to 4. With People per team the number of teams is rounded up and everyone is spread evenly, so 12 names in teams of 5 makes 3 teams of 4.
team-generator.q4: Can two people have the same name?
team-generator.a4: Yes. Every line counts as one person, so add an initial if you need to tell them apart in the result.
team-generator.a5: No. The list stays in this tab and is not saved. Copy the result to share it.

screen-resolution.a1: The large number at the top is your screen's resolution in real pixels. It is the screen size the browser reports multiplied by the device pixel ratio.
screen-resolution.q2: Why is it different from my monitor's specification?
screen-resolution.a2: With display scaling (for example 125% or 150% in Windows, or a Retina Mac) the browser lays out pages in CSS pixels. 1920 × 1080 at 125% is reported as 1536 × 864 CSS pixels. Browser zoom also changes the pixel ratio, so reset zoom to 100% for the true figure.
screen-resolution.a3: The part of the browser window that shows the page, in CSS pixels. It changes as you resize the window and is what responsive web designs use.
screen-resolution.q4: What is the device pixel ratio?
screen-resolution.a4: How many real pixels make up one CSS pixel. 1 is a standard screen, 2 or 3 is common on phones and Retina screens, and 1.25 or 1.5 means display scaling is on.
screen-resolution.q5: Is anything sent to a server?
screen-resolution.a5: No. The values are read by your browser in this tab and are not saved or uploaded.

alarm.q1: How do I set an alarm online?
alarm.a1: Pick a time, choose a sound and press Set alarm. The page shows how long until it rings. Press Test sound first to check the volume.
alarm.q2: Will it ring if the tab is in the background?
alarm.a2: Yes, while the tab stays open and the computer is awake. The sound is queued in the browser's audio engine, so a background tab still rings on time. Closing the tab, sleep mode or a locked phone can stop it.
alarm.a3: Yes. When it rings, press Snooze 5 min or Snooze 10 min, or Stop. It stops by itself after 10 minutes.
alarm.a4: Check the volume and that the tab or site is not muted. Some phones mute web audio in silent mode. The alarm must be set with a tap or click, as browsers only allow sound after one.
alarm.a5: No. It lives in this tab only. Nothing is uploaded, and reloading the page clears it.

white-noise.q1: What is the difference between white, pink and brown noise?
white-noise.a1: White noise has equal energy at every frequency and sounds like hiss. Pink noise drops 3 dB per octave and sounds like steady rain. Brown noise drops 6 dB per octave and sounds like a low roar or distant surf. Green noise is centred on the middle of the range, around 500 Hz.
white-noise.q2: Which noise is best for sleep?
white-noise.a2: There is no single best one. Many people find pink or brown noise softer than white noise. Try each at a low volume for a few minutes and keep the one you notice least.
white-noise.q3: How does the sleep timer work?
white-noise.a3: Pick 15 minutes to 8 hours before pressing Play. The sound fades out over the last 30 seconds and stops. The fade is scheduled in the browser's audio engine, so it ends on time even in a background tab.
white-noise.a4: Keep the volume low, put the speaker well away from the cot and use the sleep timer. A 2014 study in Pediatrics found that some infant sound machines can pass 85 dB at full volume; hospital nurseries are kept under about 50 dB. You can check the level with the cv.cm decibel meter.
white-noise.q5: Does it need the internet or upload anything?
white-noise.a5: The noise is generated in your browser, so once the page has loaded it plays without any download. Nothing is uploaded.

decibel-meter.q1: How accurate is an online decibel meter?
decibel-meter.a1: It gives a useful estimate, often within a few dB after calibration, but it is not a certified sound level meter. Phone and laptop microphones differ and are less sensitive at very low and very high levels.
decibel-meter.a2: Decibels with A-weighting, which turns down low and very high frequencies the way human hearing does. Noise limits and hearing safety guidelines are usually given in dB(A). Choose Z (unweighted) to see the flat level.
decibel-meter.a3: Put a real sound level meter next to your device, play a steady sound, and change Calibration until both read the same. The offset is saved in this browser. Without a meter, compare with a known source such as a quiet room (about 30–40 dB).
decibel-meter.a4: Long exposure above 85 dB(A) can damage hearing. NIOSH recommends at most 8 hours at 85 dB(A), halving the time for every 3 dB more: 4 hours at 88, 1 hour at 94, 15 minutes at 100.
decibel-meter.q5: Is the sound recorded or uploaded?
decibel-meter.a5: No. The microphone signal is analysed in this tab and thrown away. Nothing is recorded, stored or uploaded.

voice-recorder.q1: How do I record my voice online?
voice-recorder.a1: Press Record and allow the microphone. Speak, press Pause if you need a break, then Stop recording. The take appears in the list, where you can play it and download it.
voice-recorder.a2: Chrome, Edge and Firefox record WebM (Opus), Safari records M4A (AAC). Download WAV converts the take to uncompressed audio that every editor and phone can open. WAV is offered for takes up to 30 minutes.
voice-recorder.a3: One take can be up to 120 minutes. Recordings are kept in this tab's memory, so very long takes on an old phone may run out of room.
voice-recorder.q4: Are my recordings uploaded or saved?
voice-recorder.a4: No. They stay in this tab until you download them. Closing or reloading the page deletes them, and the page asks first if a take has not been downloaded.
voice-recorder.q5: How do I get clearer sound?
voice-recorder.a5: Keep Voice cleanup on to reduce background noise and echo, hold the microphone 15–30 cm from your mouth, and record in a small soft room. Turn cleanup off for music, so the instrument is not treated as noise.

screen-recorder.q1: How do I record my screen online?
screen-recorder.a1: Press Start recording, choose the entire screen, a window or a browser tab, and press Share. Press Stop recording (or the browser's Stop sharing) when done, then Download.
screen-recorder.a2: Yes. With System or tab audio on, Chrome and Edge record the sound of a shared tab, and of the whole screen on Windows and ChromeOS. Firefox and Safari record the picture only. Turn on Microphone to add your voice; it is mixed with the other sound into one track.
screen-recorder.q3: Does it work on a phone?
screen-recorder.a3: No. Phone and tablet browsers do not let web pages capture the screen. Use the built-in screen recording: Control Center on iPhone and iPad, Quick Settings on Android.
screen-recorder.a4: Auto saves MP4 where the browser can write it (Safari, recent Chrome and Edge), otherwise WebM. MP4 plays almost everywhere; WebM plays in browsers, VLC and most editors.
screen-recorder.q5: Is there a watermark or upload?
screen-recorder.a5: No watermark and no upload. The video is recorded in this tab and only leaves it when you press Download. One recording can be up to 60 minutes.

triangle.q1: How do I solve a triangle?
triangle.a1: Enter three values, at least one of them a side: three sides (SSS), two sides and the angle between them (SAS), two angles and a side (ASA or AAS), or two sides and another angle (SSA). For a right triangle, two values are enough.
triangle.q2: How are the sides and angles labelled?
triangle.a2: Side a is opposite angle A, b opposite B and c opposite C. In a right triangle C is the right angle, so c is the hypotenuse.
triangle.a3: Two sides and an angle that is not between them (SSA) can fit two different triangles, one with an acute angle and one with an obtuse angle. The calculator shows both.
triangle.a4: Area = ½ × b × c × sin A, which gives the same result as Heron's formula. For a right triangle that is ½ × a × b.
triangle.a5: Angles are in degrees. Sides can be in any unit, as long as all of them use the same one; the area is in that unit squared.

gif-maker.q1: How do I make a GIF from pictures?
gif-maker.a1: Drop two or more pictures, put them in order with the arrows, pick a delay per frame and press Make GIF. The preview plays at the delay you chose. Download saves the GIF.
gif-maker.q2: Can I turn a video into a GIF?
gif-maker.a2: Yes. Drop one video your browser can play (MP4, WebM, and MOV in Safari), set the start and end in seconds and the frame rate, then press Make GIF. Keep clips short: 300 frames is the limit, for example 30 seconds at 10 frames per second.
gif-maker.q3: Why is my GIF file so big?
gif-maker.a3: GIF stores every frame with at most 256 colours and compresses poorly compared with video. Make it smaller with a narrower width, fewer frames per second, a shorter clip, fewer colours or dithering off.
gif-maker.a4: It mixes nearby palette colours in a fine pattern so gradients and photos look smooth instead of banded. It usually makes the file a little bigger. Turn it off for flat graphics and screenshots.
gif-maker.q5: Is anything uploaded? Is there a watermark?
gif-maker.a5: No and no. Frames are drawn and encoded in this tab, so your pictures and videos never leave the device, and the GIF has no watermark.

image-splitter.q1: How do I split a picture into a 9-post grid for Instagram?
image-splitter.a1: Drop the picture and choose 3 × 3 Instagram grid. Its tiles are 3:4, the shape Instagram's profile grid shows, so the nine posts line up with no gaps; the centre is cropped to fit. Press Split, then download the ZIP or each tile.
image-splitter.q2: In what order do I post the tiles?
image-splitter.a2: Instagram puts the newest post first, top left, so post the last tile first. Tick Show posting order to number the tiles that way: post 1, then 2, up to the last.
image-splitter.q3: Can I split a panorama into a swipeable carousel?
image-splitter.a3: Yes. Choose 1 × 3 carousel (or set 1 row and as many columns as you want). Its slides are square; pick Whole picture under Tile shape to keep the full height.
image-splitter.a4: PNG tiles are copied pixel for pixel. JPG and WebP are re-encoded at high quality, which keeps files smaller. The tiles are never scaled up or down.
image-splitter.a5: No. The picture is cut in this tab and the tiles are made on your device.

area.q1: How do I find the area of a rectangle?
area.a1: Multiply length by width. A room 5 m long and 3 m wide has an area of 15 m². Pick Rectangle, type both sizes and the calculator shows the area, the perimeter and the working.
area.q2: What is the formula for the area of a circle?
area.a2: A = π × r², where r is the radius (half the diameter). A circle with a 2 cm radius has an area of about 12.566 cm².
area.q3: How do I find the area of a triangle without the height?
area.a3: Choose Triangle (three sides). It uses Heron's formula: with p = (a + b + c) / 2, A = √(p(p − a)(p − b)(p − c)). A 3-4-5 triangle has an area of 6.
area.q4: How do I convert square metres to square feet or acres?
area.a4: The result is listed in every common unit. 1 m² is about 10.764 ft²; one acre is 43,560 ft² (about 4,046.86 m²); one hectare is 10,000 m².
area.q5: Why is there no perimeter for some shapes?
area.a5: A triangle from base and height, a trapezoid and a parallelogram can have many different side lengths with the same area, so the perimeter is not fixed by those inputs.

volume.q1: How do I calculate the volume of a box?
volume.a1: Multiply length × width × height. A box 30 × 20 × 10 cm holds 6,000 cm³, which is 6 litres.
volume.q2: What is the volume of a cylinder?
volume.a2: V = π × r² × h. A can with a 4 cm radius and 10 cm height holds about 502.65 cm³, or half a litre.
volume.q3: How do I convert cubic centimetres to litres or gallons?
volume.a3: 1,000 cm³ is 1 litre and 1 cm³ is 1 mL. A US gallon is 3.785 litres (231 in³) and an imperial gallon is 4.546 litres. Every result is listed in those units.
volume.q4: What is the volume of a sphere?
volume.a4: V = 4/3 × π × r³. A ball with a 3 cm radius has a volume of about 113.1 cm³ and a surface area of about 113.1 cm² (the two numbers match only at r = 3).
volume.q5: Is the ellipsoid surface area exact?
volume.a5: No. There is no simple exact formula, so the calculator uses Knud Thomsen's approximation, within about 1% for any ellipsoid, and marks it with ≈. The volume is exact.

random-letter.q1: How do I pick a random letter?
random-letter.a1: Press Draw. Each of the 26 letters is equally likely. Draw again for a new one; the last ten draws are listed below.
random-letter.q2: Can I draw only vowels or only consonants?
random-letter.a2: Yes. Set Letters to Vowels (A E I O U) or Consonants. Add letters to Leave out, for example Q X Z for a word game.
random-letter.q3: How do I get several letters with no repeats?
random-letter.a3: Set How many and tick No repeats. Up to the whole alphabet can be drawn that way, which also gives you the letters in a random order.
random-letter.a4: Each draw uses the browser's cryptographic random generator (Web Crypto) with rejection sampling, so no letter is favoured.
random-letter.a5: English A–Z, Spanish with Ñ, the 29-letter Vietnamese alphabet, Greek, Russian (33 letters), and Japanese hiragana and katakana (46 basic kana).

word-unscrambler.a1: Type the letters into the box, in any order. Every English word they spell appears straight away, longest first, grouped by length. Each letter is used at most as many times as you typed it.
word-unscrambler.q2: How do I enter a blank tile?
word-unscrambler.a2: Type ? (or *) for each blank. A blank stands for any one letter, and the letters it filled in are marked in the results. Up to three blanks are allowed.
word-unscrambler.q3: Can I find words that start or end with certain letters?
word-unscrambler.a3: Yes. Use Starts with, Contains and Ends with, and choose an exact length. Those letters must be among the ones you typed (a blank can stand for them).
word-unscrambler.a4: ENABLE, a public-domain list of 172,823 English words widely used by word games. Proper nouns and abbreviations are not in it, and a few newer words may be missing.
word-unscrambler.q5: Is it an anagram solver too?
word-unscrambler.a5: Yes. Words that use every letter you typed are anagrams; their group is labelled Uses every letter.

concrete.q1: How much concrete do I need for a slab?
concrete.a1: Multiply length × width × thickness. A 10 × 10 ft slab 4 in thick is 33.3 ft³, or 1.23 yd³. Add 5–10% for spillage and uneven ground; the calculator adds 10% unless you change Waste.
concrete.q2: How many bags of concrete make a cubic yard?
concrete.a2: About 45 bags of 80 lb, 60 of 60 lb or 90 of 40 lb, since an 80 lb bag yields roughly 0.60 ft³. The calculator rounds bags up to whole bags.
concrete.q3: Can I mix feet and inches?
concrete.a3: Yes. Each size has its own unit, so you can give the length in feet and the thickness in inches, or metres and centimetres.
concrete.q4: How is the volume of stairs worked out?
concrete.a4: Each step is a block as deep as one run and as tall as all the steps up to it: width × run × rise × (1 + 2 + … + n). A top platform adds width × platform depth × total height.
concrete.q5: Should I order ready-mix instead of bags?
concrete.a5: For more than about 1 yd³ (0.75 m³), ready-mix from a truck is usually cheaper and quicker than mixing 45 or more bags by hand.

graphing-calculator.q1: How do I graph a function?
graphing-calculator.a1: Type it after y =, for example x^2 - 2, 2x + 1 or sin(x). The curve appears as you type. Add more rows to compare up to six functions in different colours.
graphing-calculator.a2: Numbers, x, + − × ÷ and ^ for powers, brackets, pi and e, and functions such as sqrt, abs, sin, cos, tan, ln, log and exp. 2x and 3(x + 1) multiply without a × sign. Angles are in radians.
graphing-calculator.q3: How do I move and zoom the graph?
graphing-calculator.a3: Drag to move. Zoom with the mouse wheel, by pinching on a phone, or with the + and − buttons. Reset returns to −10 to 10.
graphing-calculator.q4: Can it find where a graph crosses the x-axis?
graphing-calculator.a4: Yes. Under the graph it lists the zeros, y-intercepts and the points where two curves cross, for the part on screen. Move or zoom to find others.
graphing-calculator.a5: Download saves what is on screen as a PNG picture, without the trace line.

piano.q1: How do I play the piano with my computer keyboard?
piano.a1: The bottom row Z X C V B N M plays the white keys of the lower octave with S D G H J for the black keys; Q W E R T Y U plays the next octave with 2 3 5 6 7. Hold Space for the sustain pedal.
piano.a2: Yes. Press several keys at once on the computer keyboard, or use several fingers on a touch screen. Some keyboards cannot send more than a few keys pressed together.
piano.q3: How do I change the octave?
piano.a3: Use the ◀ and ▶ buttons above the keys. The keyboard shows one to four octaves, and the computer keys follow the lowest octave on screen.
piano.q4: Can I record what I play?
piano.a4: Yes. Press Record, play, then Stop. Play repeats your take on the same sound. The take stays on the page until you clear it or leave.
piano.a5: Turn up the volume and check that the phone is not on silent; on iPhone the ring/silent switch mutes web audio. Sound starts on your first key press.

slope.q1: How do I find the slope from two points?
slope.a1: Slope is rise over run: m = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁). For (1, 2) and (4, 8), m = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Type the two points and the calculator shows each step.
slope.a2: Yes: 3/4, −1/2 or a mixed number such as 1 1/2, as well as decimals. Results are exact fractions, with the decimal beside them.
slope.q3: What does an undefined slope mean?
slope.a3: The two points have the same x, so the line is vertical: the run is zero and you cannot divide by it. Its equation is x = that value.
slope.q4: Which forms of the line equation does it give?
slope.a4: Slope-intercept y = mx + b, point-slope y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) and standard form Ax + By = C with whole numbers.
slope.q5: What else does it work out?
slope.a5: The angle of the line, the slope as a percent grade, the distance between the points (also as a square root when exact), the midpoint and both intercepts.

sudoku.a1: Fill the 9 × 9 grid so that every row, every column and every 3 × 3 box holds each digit from 1 to 9 exactly once. The black digits are given and cannot change; yours are pink.
sudoku.q2: How do I enter numbers and notes?
sudoku.a2: Tap a cell, then a number on the pad, or type 1–9 on a keyboard. Turn on Notes (or press N) to pencil in small candidates instead. Erase or Backspace clears a cell.
sudoku.q3: What is the difference between the levels?
sudoku.a3: Easy puzzles can be finished by spotting cells with only one possible digit. Medium also needs a digit with only one place left in a row, column or box. Hard and expert need more advanced steps and have fewer given digits.
sudoku.q4: Does every puzzle have one solution?
sudoku.a4: Yes. Each puzzle is checked when it is made and has exactly one solution, so you never have to guess.
sudoku.a5: Yes, in this browser only. Close the page and come back later to carry on with the same puzzle, notes and time. Nothing is sent to cv.cm.

tic-tac-toe.a1: Two players take turns placing X and O on a 3 × 3 grid. The first to get three in a row, across, down or diagonally, wins. If the grid fills with no line, it is a draw.
tic-tac-toe.a2: On easy and medium, yes. On hard the computer plays perfectly, so the best you can do is a draw.
tic-tac-toe.a3: X always moves first. Choose Play as O to let the computer start.
tic-tac-toe.q4: Can two people play on one device?
tic-tac-toe.a4: Yes. Choose Two players and take turns tapping the grid.
tic-tac-toe.q5: What is the best first move?
tic-tac-toe.a5: A corner. It gives the other player the most ways to go wrong; the centre is the safest reply.

color-blindness-test.q1: How does the color blindness test work?
color-blindness-test.a1: Each plate is a circle of coloured dots with a number made of dots in a different colour. The two colours differ only in what one type of cone in the eye sees, so someone who lacks that cone cannot find the number.
color-blindness-test.q2: What do protan, deutan and tritan mean?
color-blindness-test.a2: Protan means the red-sensitive cones are missing or weak, deutan the green-sensitive ones (the most common kind), and tritan the blue-sensitive ones. Protan and deutan together are red–green color blindness.
color-blindness-test.a3: No. Screens show colours differently and this test is not calibrated, so it can only point to a possible deficiency. An optometrist or ophthalmologist can test you properly.
color-blindness-test.q4: How accurate is an online color blindness test?
color-blindness-test.a4: It works best on a good screen at full brightness, with night mode, blue-light filters and colour filters turned off. Take it again on another screen if the result surprises you.
color-blindness-test.a5: No. The plates are drawn for cv.cm on the same principle, with new random numbers and dot layouts every time you retake the test.

military-time.q1: How do I convert military time to standard time?
military-time.a1: From 1300 on, subtract 12 from the hours and add PM: 1430 is 2:30 PM. From 0100 to 1159 it is the same time with AM. 1200 is 12:00 PM (noon) and 0000 is 12:00 AM (midnight).
military-time.q2: How do I say military time?
military-time.a2: Read the four digits as two pairs: 1430 is "fourteen thirty hours". Whole hours use "hundred": 0800 is "zero eight hundred hours". A leading zero is said as "zero".
military-time.a3: 0000 is the start of a day. Some people write 2400 for the end of the day, which is the same moment as 0000 the next day.
military-time.a4: Zulu time is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), written with a Z, such as 1430Z. The page shows the current Zulu time next to your local time.
military-time.a5: Four digits (1430), 24-hour time with a colon (14:30), or 12-hour time with AM or PM (2:30 pm). It works both ways.

height-calculator.q1: How can I predict my child's adult height?
height-calculator.a1: Add both parents' heights, add 13 cm (5 in) for a boy or subtract 13 cm for a girl, and halve it. Most children end up within 8.5 cm (about 3.5 in) of that figure.
height-calculator.q2: What does the growth chart method add?
height-calculator.a2: Give your child's age and height, and the calculator finds their percentile on the CDC growth charts and the adult height on the same percentile at age 20.
height-calculator.q3: How accurate is a height prediction?
height-calculator.a3: It is an estimate. Genes set a range; nutrition, sleep, health and the timing of puberty decide where in it a child ends up. A child who matures early can look tall for their age and finish average.
height-calculator.q4: Which ages does it work for?
height-calculator.a4: The growth chart part works from 2 to 20 years. The parents' method works at any age.
height-calculator.q5: When should I talk to a doctor?
height-calculator.a5: If your child's height drops across percentile lines, or is far below the parents' target range, ask a paediatrician.
